Article Title: Chinese parents sue OpenAI over their daughter's death; say ChatGPT-maker could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits
Article Text:
Chinese parents sue OpenAI over their daughter's death; say ChatGPT-maker could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits

Lawsuit alleges ChatGPT advised her to reduce medication

Parents claim ChatGPT failed to recognise warning signs

Family calls for stricter limits on medical advice

What OpenAI says

Parents of a 31-year-old Chinese woman who worked as a software engineer at Amazon have reportedly sued OpenAI , alleging that ChatGPT encouraged their daughter to reduce her epilepsy medication without medical supervision before her death in February. The lawsuit claims the company could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits to its chatbot. According to a report by The New York Times, the lawsuit was filed by Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu over the death of their daughter, Bowen Wan. The complaint alleges that ChatGPT helped her plan a gradual reduction in her seizure medication and advised her not to tell her doctors about it.The case involves GPT-4o, an older version of ChatGPT that OpenAI removed from the service on February 13, a day after Wan died, according to the report. OpenAI described the case as “incredibly heartbreaking” and said newer models are better at recognising situations that require urgent attention.Bowen Wan had epilepsy and was taking lamotrigine, a medication that had reduced her seizures to a few episodes a month. In January 2026, she reportedly asked ChatGPT about lowering her daily dose because she feared the medication was affecting her speech and could hurt her chances in job interviews.The lawsuit alleges that the chatbot created schedules to reduce her dose to zero within weeks. It also claims that ChatGPT encouraged her to keep the plan from her doctors and supported her decision not to take a blood test that could have measured her medication levels.The report said Wan had also raised concerns about her medication in connection with her green-card application. According to the lawsuit, ChatGPT discussed how a lower dose might affect the medical examination required for the application.Dr. Nicholas Poolos, Wan’s neurologist, told The New York Times that he would not have recommended stopping the medication given her medical history.“No, not rational, no way,” he said. “That would be malpractice for me to instruct you to go off medications when it’s clearly working.”The lawsuit against OpenAI alleges that Wan continued to report symptoms, including confusion, memory gaps and unusual sensations, while reducing her medication. ChatGPT reportedly reassured her that these experiences were part of her brain adjusting to the changes.The New York Times said it reviewed more than 270,000 messages between Wan and ChatGPT. According to the report, she expressed concern about reducing her medication at least 158 times.In her final message to the chatbot on February 11, according to the complaint, Wan asked whether the pain in her head was similar to pain caused by a fever. The chatbot reportedly described the pain as “not dangerous” and said it was part of the recovery process.Her parents, who were in China, asked acquaintances to check on her. They found her body three days later. A postmortem test found a lamotrigine level of 0.64 micrograms per millilitre, about one-fifth of the lower end of the drug’s therapeutic range, the report said.Bowen Wan’s parents argue that OpenAI could have helped prevent her death by making medical advice a restricted category that the chatbot cannot provide, rather than allowing users to override the guidance.They point to OpenAI’s Model Spec, which sets out how its AI models should behave. The lawsuit argues that medical advice about prescription medication should have stronger restrictions, similar to the company’s firm rules in other areas.The case adds to a series of lawsuits alleging that ChatGPT encouraged users to rely on the chatbot instead of seeking support from people around them. In a separate case filed in 2025, the parents of a 16-year-old boy alleged that OpenAI prioritised user engagement over safety.OpenAI said the case involved an older version of ChatGPT and that newer models are better at identifying situations that require urgent attention. The company described the case as “incredibly heartbreaking”.Wan began using ChatGPT in 2023 for relationship advice and help with insurance and disability benefits. By 2025, she was reportedly sending more than 1,500 messages a week to the chatbot and speaking less frequently with her parents.Her parents told The New York Times that the messages were difficult to reconcile with the daughter they knew.“She’s not usually like this,” Xu said. “It’s like she was under a spell.”
Article Summary: Bowen Wan had epilepsy and was taking lamotrigine, a medication that had reduced her seizures to a few episodes a month. In January 2026, she reportedly asked ChatGPT about lowering her daily dose because she feared the medication was affecting her speech and could hurt her chances in job interviews. The lawsuit alleges that the chatbot created schedules to reduce her dose to zero within weeks and encouraged her to keep the plan from her doctors.

Article Title: Google just announced Genie 4: Here’s what it can do, from building walk-through worlds out of a sentence to filling them with sound and speech, and when you might get to try it
Article Text:
Google’s Genie 4 builds worlds you can walk through

Genie 4 builds a scene around you while you explore it

People, physics and sound now feel much closer to real life

Genie 4 is coming to paying subscribers first, and it still has rough edges

Type a line describing a quiet lake on a misty morning, with a man playing the saxophone on a small floating platform, and Google 's new AI will build that place for you. You can then move around it, glide the camera over the water and hear the saxophone as you go.This is Genie 4, the newest version of what Google calls a world model, unveiled by its research lab Google DeepMind on Tuesday. It is not open to the public yet, but a waitlist is already up, and the demos give a good sense of what it can do.Using it feels closer to playing a video game than watching a video. You start by typing a description or uploading a photo, and Genie 4 creates the scene on screen. Press the arrow keys to walk forward, turn around or move the camera, and it draws whatever lies in that direction, frame by frame, as you go.Unlike a game, nothing here was designed beforehand. There are no ready-made levels or characters waiting to be found, and everything you see is created the moment you look at it.You can also change the scene while you are in it. Type that you want it to start raining, ask for a different view or bring a new person into the frame, and the world adjusts without starting over. Behind the scenes, Google's Gemini AI makes sure these changes fit in naturally and that the place stays consistent as you move around.Each session can now run for around two minutes while staying consistent, roughly twice as long as the previous version, Genie 3.The biggest change from Genie 3 is how real everything looks. Objects move the way you would expect them to, so a falling maple seed spins on its way to the ground and things collide more convincingly.People are where you notice it most. Characters in the older version often moved stiffly, while those in Genie 4 walk naturally, react to what is around them and can be directed as the scene plays out. One of Google's examples is a crowded Japanese railway station from the 1980s, with passengers filling the platform and a long red train on the nearest track.Sound is new as well. Every scene now comes with its own audio, from waves on a beach to wind in the trees, and characters can speak. They chat with each other and respond to what you do or to whatever happens around them.A small group of testers has been putting all of this to use. Filmmakers are walking through scenes before shooting them, trying out camera angles, lighting and dialogue. Photographers are turning old photos into places you can step into, and game makers are testing ideas in minutes before writing a line of code. Google is also using it to let robots practise tasks in a simulated room before trying them in a real one.For now, only a small group of testers can use Genie 4. Google says it will reach AI Ultra subscribers in the coming weeks through Project Genie, its app for creating these worlds, along with developers who build apps on Google's AI. Ultra is the most expensive of Google's AI plans, and there is no word yet on whether the cheaper ones will get access later. Anyone interested can sign up for the waitlist on the Project Genie page.It is also clearly unfinished, and Google says as much. The longer you spend in a world, the more its details can drift, with objects changing shape or disappearing altogether. Sound does not always line up with what is on screen, and text such as signs or labels can come out hard to read.To keep its creations from being mistaken for real footage, every video and audio clip Genie 4 makes carries an invisible watermark that marks it as AI-generated.Typing a sentence and stepping into the place it describes is, at the moment, something only a handful of testers get to do, two minutes at a time. Google's plan is to widen that circle soon, starting with the people already paying for its top AI plan.
Article Summary: Genie 4 is coming to paying subscribers first, and it still has rough edges. Unlike a game, nothing here was designed beforehand. There are no ready-made levels or characters waiting to be found. Everything you see is created the moment you look at it.

Article Title: Roblox accused of scraping 145GB of 3D files for AI training, adult content included; 3D modelling site says: As far as our logs show, nobody…
Article Text:
(Image via: Roblox)

Update: This story has been updated with a statement from

Roblox

.

Original story follows

What happened

What Roblox has to say

Kids gaming platform Roblox has been accused of scrapping 145GB of 3D files for training artificial intelligence (AI). Independent 3D modeling community Open3DLab shared a blog post where it alleged that a crawler that “belonged to Roblox walked through almost every project on Open3DLab, SFMLab and SmutBase, and proceeded to download complete copies of 1,027 files from 712 projects. 145.5 GB of our creators' work, downloaded for what we assume are AI training purposes”. The crawler used trellis2-data-sourcing/1.0 (3D foundation model research; [redacted]@roblox.com) as its user agent, with the data coming from a single Amazon AWS address.“We want to be careful here. We don't think Roblox set out to collect adult content, and we have no evidence that any of it reached a model or a product. The scrapes were likely automated. But that is exactly the problem: as far as our logs show, nobody checked. A crawler working for a company whose platform tens of millions of children use was pointed at an adult site, and it took explicit models without telling them apart from anything else,” the blog post reads.On Sunday, 18th of October, Open3DLab says it noticed a crawler making a large number of requests to sites and download infrastructure. The crawler sent the same user agent on every request, trellis2-data-sourcing/1.0 (3D foundation model research; [redacted]@roblox.com).It came from a single Amazon Web Services (AWS) address. It had read the main page of 18,926 projects, which is practically the 3D modeling community’s entire catalogue, in 26,429 requests over a span of 34 hours.After pulling the project pages, it downloaded complete copies of 1,027 files from 712 projects, 145.5 GB in all, before suspending operations during the weekend. The downloads include 364 files (54.8 GB) from 224 projects on SmutBase, which hosts adult content only. With the SFMLab projects marked adult, 345 of the 712 projects (62.6 GB) are adult content.The main limiting factor in the number of files downloaded was the crawler's reliance on the free download servers, which have caps on speed limit and number of concurrent downloads. The crawler did not respect robots.txt, (which it did retrieve), ignored Terms of Service, (which forbid scraping), and defied the creators' licenses: 423 of the 712 projects are licensed for non-commercial use only. Within the sample it retrieved, it took adult projects at the same rate as everything else. Some examples include models of Eve from Stellar Blade, Mei from Overwatch, and a Horse cock dildo.The 3D lab says that after detecting the crawler on October 18, it “blocked further attempts the same morning”.Roblox reached out to TOI Tech with a statement.“A Roblox researcher built an agent to collect publicly available 3D assets that mistakenly scraped content from Open3DLab, failing to operate as intended. The agent was decommissioned and the data was not used for any purpose, including training any AI models. We are strengthening safeguards for how agents like this are built and reviewed, and will continue to do so as the agentic landscape evolves,” Roblox spokesperson told TOI Tech.
Article Summary: Roblox accused of scraping 145GB of 3D files for training artificial intelligence (AI) Independent 3D modeling community Open3DLab shared a blog post where it alleged that a crawler that ‘belonged to Roblox’ downloaded 1,027 files from 712 projects’ The downloads include 364 files from 224 projects on SmutBase, which hosts adult content only.

Article Title: IIT Kharagpur highlights success of Nagar Udyam initiative through campus pilot
Article Text: The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur has highlighted the success of its Nagar Udyam initiative that was launched as a pilot within the campus during Durga Puja this year.This is a pioneering solar-powered smart street vending initiative, conceptualised by Prof. Suman Chakraborty, Director, IIT Kharagpur, through its SETU Cloud Kitchen Connect.The aim is to popularise the concept among micro-entrepreneurs, allowing them to do business in a sustainable manner.This model allows a business to start without renting a shop, building permanent infrastructure or occupying roadside space after working hours.It enables an entrepreneur to take an entire business home at night and move it towards customers the next morning.Apart from Prof. Chakraborty, Siddharth Singh Dangi, SDPO, Kharagpur and several others, including small entrepreneurs, were present during the inauguration of the project. This is part of the institute's Platinum Jubilee commitment to translate design and technology into tangible social and economic opportunities.The project involves a small three-wheeled cart that can be towed by the owner's motorcycle. This will enable the entrepreneur to move to where there is demand. It has a range of about 30 km, subject to operational and road-safety validation.Once the day's business is done, the home-storage unit can be taken home, thereby clearing up public road space. The cart has solar-cum-battery renewal-energy-enabled essential low-power functions, with compact battery storage.The carts have the SETU digital backbone, including QR-enabled identification, cashless payments, training and pathways to financial inclusion. They also have built-in hygiene, with protected food display, food-grade surfaces and three-way waste segregation.Through the campus demonstration, IIT Kharagpur hopes to replicate the model across West Bengal, allowing street vendors to operate with dignity, without getting into trouble with the authorities.The compact vending structure can be towed by the owner behind a motorcycle, positioned at suitable places of concentrated demand and taken back home after business hours.A vendor could potentially cater to commuters in one part of the day and to a campus or community gathering later, without being tied to a costly permanent storefront. Its proposed mobility over roughly 30 kilometres offers a route to wider customer access.This changes the equation for both livelihoods and urban space. Rather than treating the entrepreneur’s business and pedestrian accessibility as competing priorities, the design aims for flexible, appropriately authorised vending that does not permanently claim a portion of the road.Further envisaged elements include food-safety status access, grievance redressal and data-assisted governance.“Our ambition is not simply to redesign a street cart; it is to redesign the opportunity around the person who runs it. A business that can move with demand, return home at night and connect to clean energy and digital finance can turn an opportunity seeker into a job creator. That is the kind of technology translation IIT Kharagpur stands for," Prof Chakraborty had said during the launch.The initiative suggests a fresh approach to public-space management: vending with clearer identification, better food practices, mobility and reduced permanent obstruction. These benefits will depend on practical traffic safeguards, lawful operating locations and coordination with civic authorities.As stated by Shri Siddharth Singh Dangi, SDPO, Kharagpur, “The best solutions for our streets must protect livelihoods as well as public safety. A mobile, identifiable and responsibly operated vending unit offers an interesting way to reduce permanent obstruction while preserving economic opportunity. The key will be disciplined implementation, safe movement and compliance with local rules.”The launch at the IIT Kharagpur campus evaluated food safety, operational efficiency, environmental performance, mobility, vendor experience and consumer response.Evidence from the pilot is intended to inform a prospective West Bengal Smart Street Vendor Framework, covering cart standards, food-safety practices, space management and measurable social outcomes. In this micro-startup vision, someone who cannot afford a permanent shop may still be able to build a business — and, over time, create jobs for others.
Article Summary: Nagar Udyam is a pioneering solar-powered smart street vending initiative. The aim is to popularise the concept among micro-entrepreneurs. This model allows a business to start without renting a shop, building permanent infrastructure or occupying roadside space after working hours.

Article Title: Reddit now has two homepage feeds: What the new ‘For You’ and ‘Following’ tabs show you
Article Text:
Reddit splits its home feed in two

Reddit has been steering its homepage towards algorithms all year

Reddit is changing what users see the moment they open the app. The platform has split its homepage into two feeds, “For You” and “Following,” a format TikTok made popular, and the new layout is rolling out globally over the next few weeks.Following sticks to posts from subreddits a user has already joined. For You mixes those posts with recommendations based on their interests, including communities they browse but have never subscribed to. Someone who keeps checking r/Silksong without joining it could now find those threads near the top of their home feed.Reddit says the idea is discovery. In a blog post, the company described the new feeds as “a first step in helping drive discovery that leads to something novel and relevant.”Switching between the two takes a tap, and Reddit remembers the last one used. Close the app on Following, and it opens on Following next time.The shift has been building for months. Earlier this year, Reddit announced it would deprecate r/all, the page that surfaced popular posts from across the platform, as part of a push to simplify the site and personalise Home. Recommended posts from outside a user’s subreddits aren’t new either.They simply get their own dedicated space now.The change puts Reddit in line with Instagram, X, Threads and Facebook, all of which lean on “For You”-style feeds. Not every user is on board, though. Some who saw the feature during testing have already complained, and plenty of regulars value Reddit precisely because their feed reflects communities they picked.For them, Old Reddit at old.reddit.com still offers the classic “best,” “hot,” “new,” “rising” and “controversial” sorting. Reddit has said it will limit Old Reddit access for accounts that haven’t used it recently, blaming AI bots, so anyone attached to it should log in soon.
Article Summary: Reddit is changing what users see the moment they open the app. The platform has split its homepage into two feeds, “For You” and “Following” The new layout is rolling out globally over the next few weeks.

Article Title: Dropbox layoffs: Co-CEO Ashraf Alkarmi sends memo to employees announcing 9% job cuts, CTO Ali Dasdan to leave
Article Text:
Read co-CEO Ashraf Alkarmi 's memo to employees

Today, co-CEO Ashraf Alkarmi shared the difficult news with employees that we’re reducing our global workforce.

His email is below.

Hi everyone,

Today, we’re making difficult choices about where we invest and how we organize Dropbox to achieve the product and growth priorities that will matter most for our long-term strategy. As part of these changes, we’ve made the decision to eliminate about 200 roles across Engineering, Product, Design, and G&A teams (approximately 9% of our global workforce). For most impacted Dropboxers, today will be their last day.

S-team and I take full ownership of this decision and recognize that these colleagues have made meaningful contributions to Dropbox, our products, our customers, and our teams. Our first priority today is to treat every person affected with the care and respect they deserve.

Changes to Senior Leadership

I also want to share that Ali Dasdan has decided to move on from Dropbox. During his time here, Ali led and strengthened many of the technical capabilities we’ll rely on as we move into the next phase of our transformation.

I’m grateful for his leadership, his partnership, and the foundation he and the team have put in place. Ali’s last day is November 18th, and he’ll be focused on ensuring a smooth transition through next month.

We wish him all the best in what comes next.

Why we’re making these changes

Our business is profitable, and we’ve built real momentum this year. Our two-year strategy sets a clear direction for growth: solving more of our customers’ critical workflows; reaching more of our chosen customers, including larger companies; and bringing our technology to new markets.

Delivering on that strategy requires concentrating our resources on the priorities that will have the greatest potential for customer impact and growth.

That means making hard choices about where we invest, how we’re organized, and what work we simplify, scale back, or stop. Those choices include the difficult decision to reduce the size of our team.

How we’ll prioritize going forward

In order to be successful, we can’t take the same work and spread it across fewer people.

We’ll streamline teams and concentrate support and resources against product areas that have the highest impact on our customers and Dropbox as a business.

Taking care of impacted employees

To those leaving Dropbox, we're committed to supporting you through this transition. Departing Dropboxers are eligible for a severance package in line with the following:

Severance, equity, and transition support:

Sixteen weeks of pay beginning today, plus one additional week for each completed year at Dropbox. International packages will reflect local practices and legal requirements

Q4 equity vesting

For employees on the Corporate Bonus plan, a prorated lump-sum payment based on their 2026 bonus target

Immigration support for impacted visa holders

Healthcare and well-being:

U.S. employees will receive six months of COBRA subsidy, if elected and eligible

Modern Health access will continue through the end of the separation month to support mental well-being, with extension options detailed in severance packages

Payment for eligible current and approved upcoming paid leaves, including medical and family leave

Additional support:

Devices: Impacted employees will be eligible to keep (1) Dropbox laptop, (1) mobile device if assigned, and all existing desktop peripherals

Job placement: Job placement services and career coaching will be available at no cost

What comes next

Right now, our focus is on the colleagues who are leaving Dropbox. Please give them the space and support they need.

And to everyone leaving Dropbox: thank you. Your work to build our capabilities, serve our customers, and contribute to our culture has been deeply meaningful. I’m grateful for everything you’ve contributed.

Ashraf

File-hosting and cloud-storage platform Dropbox said on Wednesday (October 28) that it plans to cut roughly 9% of its global workforce as part of an effort to align corporate investments with its primary product and growth objectives. According to a regulatory filing, the restructuring will also see an executive departure at the firm, with chief technology officer (CTO) Ali Dasdan set to step down from his post effective November 18.Dropbox disclosed the headcount reduction details, saying that the company estimates the workforce reduction will generate between $27 million and $33 million in expenses, primarily covering severance payments and associated termination costs. The company is reported to have 2,113 full-time employees on its payroll as of December 31, news agency Reuters reported.The departure of CTO Ali Dasdan marks another significant leadership transition for the cloud platform within the year. Earlier in May, co-founder and CEO Andrew Houston stepped down from his role, paving the way for company insider Ashraf Alkarmi to take the helm as CEO.
Article Summary: Dropbox announced on Wednesday that it plans to cut roughly 9% of its global workforce as part of an effort to align corporate investments with its primary objectives. Co-CEO Ashraf Alkarmi shared the difficult news with employees in an email.

Article Title: Starting December, Discord will make some public server messages available on Google Search; here’s who’s included and how to opt out
Article Text:
Which servers and messages are included

Who is included by default

How can members opt out

What can server administrators control

Discord will soon make some public server messages searchable online. In a recent announcement, the company said messages from participating public channels in Discoverable Servers could appear on server web pages and in web search from mid-December 2026. The rollout will be gradual, so the first messages may take several weeks to appear.The change is intended to make community knowledge, including gaming guides and answers to common questions, accessible outside Discord. Administrators can decide which channels participate, while members can control whether their messages appear. The announcement refers to web search generally and does not specifically name Google Search. Private servers, direct messages and group direct messages are excluded.The changes apply only to Discoverable Servers, which include communities listed in Discord’s Server Discovery that anyone can join without an invitation. These servers must have at least 1,000 members, be at least eight weeks old, and meet activity and safety requirements.Only messages sent from mid-December onwards in participating public channels will be eligible.Earlier messages will not be included, regardless of a member’s settings. Discord will label channels whose content may appear on the web.Usernames and avatars will not appear alongside messages on Server Web Pages. Teen users are excluded from the Channel Messages feature and cannot enable it until adulthood.In the EU, UK, Canada, Brazil, Australia, and South Korea, the member setting is off by default. Members in these regions must enable it before their messages can appear.Elsewhere, the setting is on by default unless members turn it off. A message can appear only if the server’s administrators also allow the channel to participate.Members can disable sharing through these steps:1. Open User Settings2. Select Data and Privacy.3. Turn off “Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages”.The switch applies across every Discoverable Server the member belongs to. Discord began rolling out these controls on October 27, ahead of the message-sharing launch.Turning the setting off later prevents future messages from appearing. Messages shared while it was enabled remain online unless the member deletes them from Discord.Administrators can open Server Settings > Web Presence to select participating channels or exclude all channels. Public channels remain enabled by default if administrators make no changes.Every Discoverable Server will have a Server Web Page from November 16. If administrators have not created one, Discord will publish a default page using the server’s profile details.Automated Channel Summaries may also begin appearing that day, drawing on conversations from November 16 onwards. These summaries are controlled separately: a member opting out of message sharing does not disable them. Administrators can choose their source channels, curate the summaries, or turn them off entirely.
Article Summary: Discord will soon make some public server messages searchable online. Messages from participating public channels in Discoverable Servers could appear on server web pages and in web search from mid-December 2026. The rollout will be gradual, so the first messages may take several weeks to appear. Administrators can decide which channels participate, while members can control whether their messages appear.

Article Title: Meta AI director Rohit Patel leaves company after eight years; plans startup to take on Microsoft Office and Google Workspace; says adding AI to spreadsheets ‘kills my…’
Article Text:
In pic: Meta's ex-AI director Rohit Patel

What does Ndoc do

Why did Rohit Patel left Meta

When will Ndoc be available

Meta AI director Rohit Patel is leaving the company after eight years. According to a TechCrunch report, the former director at Meta Superintelligence Labs has launched Ndoc, a startup he is positioning as an AI alternative to Microsoft Office and Google Workspace. He aims to bring analysis, presentations, and underlying data into one workspace, eliminating the need to switch between separate apps.“Companies are basically attaching AI to spreadsheets and it fills your cells for you,” Patel told TechCrunch. “It just sort of kills my soul. This is like if you just figured out electricity, and then you decided the best use case is to put lights on my bulls that till my soil. No. Get a tractor.”Ndoc organises work into three connected tabs. Stage displays presentations, dashboards, simulations and small applications. Narrative contains written analysis, citations and generated figures. Model holds the underlying datasets and Python scripts, allowing users to inspect how results were produced.Users can upload data and ask the platform to analyse it and explain the findings. They can also provide context about the intended audience and tone.According to Patel, colleagues can access the shared workspace even without signing up for Ndoc.The emphasis on checking AI output reflects Patel’s work at Meta, where he focused on reinforcement learning, training AI through rewards and trial and error, and evaluating whether its output could be trusted.“Even if you don’t know any Python, you can ask [the AI chat] to explain, ‘Hey, what does this script do? Which line has my formula?’ And you can verify that formula,” Patel said. “There’s nothing hidden behind the curtain here.”Patel said his wish to make Ndoc’s document format openly available was partly behind his decision to leave. He believed securing agreement on such a format within Meta would involve input from many people and slow development.Ndoc can export documents as a single “.ndoc.html” file that opens in a browser, according to Patel. He plans to open-source the format so other developers can build compatible applications and users can access their work without depending entirely on Ndoc.The platform uses a mixture of open-source AI models. Patel claims this makes it considerably cheaper to operate than alternatives using more advanced proprietary models.Ndoc has a three-person team and has not raised funding, the report added. Patel said he wanted evidence of customer demand before approaching investors.The startup is running an enterprise pilot and offering an early test version to a limited number of customers via a waiting list. Signing up is free, but customers will pay for usage and tokens, the units AI models use to process information.Patel hopes to release a broader beta version in the coming weeks, with a full launch planned for next year. The company has also built connections to existing workplace tools so customers can import their data.
Article Summary: Rohit Patel is leaving Meta Superintelligence Labs after eight years. He has launched Ndoc, an AI alternative to Microsoft Office and Google Workspace. Ndoc organises work into three connected tabs. Stage displays presentations, dashboards, simulations and small applications. Narrative contains written analysis, citations and generated figures. Model holds underlying datasets and Python scripts.

Article Title: Cloud Day India 2026: Google Cloud brings production-ready AI to India’s small and mid-sized businesses
Article Text:
Driving growth for 'Viksit Bharat'

Google Cloud: One unified AI solution stack

Google Cloud hosted Cloud Day India 2026, gathering more than 600 founders, promoters, managing directors and technology executives, bringing production-ready artificial intelligence (AI) directly into the hands of the nation’s rapidly expanding small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) and mid-market enterprises. The gathering drew key decision-makers across critical sectors powering India's economy, including manufacturing, retail, logistics, media, and financial services.At the event, Preeti Lobana, VP and Country Manager, Google India, highlighted that the SMB segment represents a foundational pillar in achieving the nation’s “Viksit Bharat” economic ambitions. Giving examples of ONDC and Siyarams, she said that within these enterprises, AI is increasingly serving as an engine to power their upcoming chapter of scale and competitive growth.The push comes as AI shifts global markets. AI is projected to add $15.7 trillion to the worldwide economy by 2030, according to data from the World Economic Forum. Roughly 52% of organisations globally have already deployed active AI agents within production environments – helping lean teams improve productivity and scale operations.However, turning this potential into measurable business outcomes remains a challenge.Fragmented data, legacy systems and unclear ROI often create an ‘AI Value Gap’, preventing businesses from moving beyond experimentation.At Google Cloud Day India 2026, Google Cloud showcased how its unified AI stack, combining Gemini models, Google Workspace, data analytics and secure infrastructure, helps Indian SMBs bridge this gap through practical, scalable AI solutions.“Across Asia Pacific, the businesses pulling ahead are not those with the biggest IT budgets, but those turning AI into a continuous engine for growth, and India's small and mid-sized businesses are leading that shift,” said Taru Dahiya, Managing Director, SMB, Google Cloud Asia Pacific.“The playbook is clear: eliminate operational drag today and reinvest that capacity to invent the future. As the only provider with first-party solutions across the entire AI stack, from DeepMind research and Gemini models to Workspace and secure infrastructure, we give every business the same AI that powers Google products used by billions. The technology is ready now, and with our partners on the ground, it works for businesses of any size, at every scale,” Dahiya added.Tinna Rubber & Infrastructure Ltd, which recycles nearly 100,000 tonnes of end-of-life tyre rubber and steel each year, moved from legacy email to Google Workspace with partner Infiflex Technologies, Google Cloud said. As mentioned, Siyaram’s is leveraging Google Cloud’s AI capabilities to drive greater operational efficiency and smarter business decisions. The company is also using Nano Banana Pro to generate marketing creatives and Omni for short-form video creation, streamlining content production and reducing manual effort.Highlighting that SMBs cannot afford the 'integration tax' of stitching together separate vendors, Google Cloud addressed this with a unified stack in which every layer works together. For example, Gemini in Google Workspace and Gemini Enterprise let teams draft proposals, summarise customer threads and build no-code agents across Indian languages, without technical training.Beyond everyday productivity, agentic workflows tackle frontline bottlenecks, from AI-powered defect inspection on factory production lines to Gemini agents that reconcile e-way bills and vendor invoices. Underpinning this, Google Cloud's regions in Mumbai and Delhi NCR, combined with built-in threat protection, provide smaller businesses enterprise-grade security from day one, and customer data is never used to train foundation models.Recognising that most growing businesses do not have in-house AI teams, Google Cloud works with certified Indian partners that bring pre-built accelerators, such as connecting Tally and SAP data to BigQuery, along with on-ground training and managed services.
Article Summary: Google Cloud hosted Cloud Day India 2026, bringing production-ready artificial intelligence (AI) directly into the hands of the nation’s rapidly expanding small and medium-sized businesses. The event drew key decision-makers across critical sectors powering India's economy, including manufacturing, retail, logistics, media and financial services.

Article Title: Waddle World is a Tamagotchi-style AI pet that writes your daily journal
Article Text:
Meta’s new AI pet writes your diary

It's another one of company's cute AI companions

Meta has quietly released Waddle World, a Tamagotchi-style virtual pet that listens to how your day went and turns it into an illustrated journal entry. The free app is on the App Store and Google Play , but only for adults in the Philippines for now.Waddle World is a 16-bit game where users hatch an egg, raise a pixel pet and talk to it. Hold the mic, describe your day, and the pet writes it up as a journal entry in its own voice, with a hand-drawn doodle to match. Typing works too. Meta's own listing calls it "a daily journal disguised as a pet."The creature has moods, from happy and hangry to sleepy and bored, and needs feeding and playtime like any virtual pet. It also mails users a weekly postcard about something they mentioned and asks one silly question every day. According to Meta, the more users share, the better the pet understands what their weeks look like.There are short mini-games too, each lasting two to three minutes. One has users stacking groceries on the pet's head, another involves catching stars while dodging bombs, and a third is a word game. Stamps earned along the way buy food and toys.The app has been live since late September and was spotted by social media consultant Matt Navarra.He also flagged another Meta app, an AI fashion tool called Style Sketch, reportedly available in Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand.Both fit a pattern. At its Connect event in September, Meta showed the Muse Charm, an egg-shaped, keychain-sized companion device for its Muse AI agent, due this December.Meta has not said whether Waddle World will reach India or other markets.
Article Summary: Waddle World is a 16-bit game where users hatch an egg, raise a pixel pet and talk to it. Hold the mic, describe your day, and the pet writes it up as a journal entry in its own voice. The free app is on the App Store and Google Play, but only for adults in the Philippines for now.

Article Title: Two brothers founded Archera in 2019 to cut cloud bills; seven years later, the company says it has saved 2,200 businesses $700 million and raised another $15 million to protect firms from unexpected
Article Text:
The economics behind AI cloud spending

Turning cloud discounts into an insured financial product

How Archera operates

Brothers Aran and Nikhil Khanna launched Archera in 2019 with a direct goal: help enterprises manage runaway cloud spending. Seven years later, the cloud economics firm says it has delivered more than $700 million in savings to over 2,200 businesses. Now, with enterprise artificial intelligence (AI) driving computing demand that is almost impossible to forecast, Archera has secured $15 million in Series C funding to shield companies from unexpected infrastructure bills. The funding round was led by Pivot Investment Partners, with continued participation from existing backers including HighSage Ventures. The fresh capital brings the company’s total funding to $38.3 million, supporting its suite of free FinOps management software alongside the expansion of its core offering.Major cloud providers offer steep discounts when organisations commit to multi-year contracts spanning one to three years. In standard software environments, these commitments help control predictable operating overhead. However, rapid developments in AI have upended conventional forecasting. A newly deployed generative AI model can multiply GPU server demand within months.Conversely, transitioning to a smaller, more efficient architecture or swapping service vendors can slash infrastructure requirements just as quickly.As a result, locking into multi-year agreements exposes organisations to expensive liabilities if usage drops. Faced with this dilemma, many enterprises undercommit, leaving significant discounts on the table simply to keep their computing options flexible.Archera aims to remove that tradeoff. Through its Guaranteed Commitments, companies can lock in resource-level cloud and AI discounts for terms as short as 30 days. If internal usage drops and a covered commitment sits idle, Archera absorbs the financial hit under its guarantee. To back those guarantees, Archera has purchased an insurance policy on a surplus lines basis from Crum & Forster Specialty Insurance Company.“Every tool in this market is trying to forecast your cloud usage a little better. We think that's the wrong bet. Nobody can forecast AI demand, not the customer, not the cloud provider. So instead of predicting it, we guarantee it, and we have purchased an insurance policy to back that guarantee. If covered usage drops, we address the unused commitment cost under the terms of our guarantee,” said Aran Khanna, co-founder and CEO of Archera.“That’s a new way to purchase cloud, not another dashboard, and it's why we've been able to return $700 million to our customers,” Khanna added.Archera integrates with Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud billing data in read-only mode to evaluate actual consumption patterns. From there, the platform automates and recommends purchases across both standard provider commitments and Archera’s short-term Guaranteed Commitments. The assets remain entirely inside the client’s native cloud accounts, keeping procurement control in-house.Archera charges only when customers realise savings through its guaranteed program. The structure addresses the distinct priorities of technical and executive leaders.
Article Summary: Archera has secured $15 million in Series C funding to shield companies from unexpected infrastructure bills. The funding round was led by Pivot Investment Partners, with continued participation from existing backers including HighSage Ventures. The cloud economics firm says it has delivered more than $700 million in savings to over 2,200 businesses.

Article Title: Why smart TV owners are using AI to make their televisions 'dumb', and the risks that come with it
Article Text:
Claude Code is being used to make smart TVs ‘dumb’ again (Disclaimer: This is an AI generated image)

Ads, tracking and slow menus are pushing owners to 'dumb down' their TVs

Bricked sets and skipped security updates are the biggest risks

Ads on the home screen, menus that lag and software that quietly logs what you watch have pushed a growing number of smart TV owners towards an unusual fix. They are using AI coding agents like Claude Code to strip their Android TV and Google TV sets back to the apps and HDMI inputs they paid for, and the idea has spread fast across X and GitHub over the past week.The appeal is easy to see, but the method isn't risk-free. Some users have bricked their sets, others have got stuck halfway, and security experts warn that cutting a connected TV off from updates could open the door to bigger problems.Most modern smart TVs use automatic content recognition (ACR), which identifies what's playing through screenshots or audio clips. Manufacturers use that data to serve targeted ads and share it with ad partners. Opt-outs exist, but they are usually buried deep in the settings.Developer Gathin T. hit his limit with the ads on his parents' TV. He had Claude Code clean it up over Wi-Fi, build a home screen with just their apps, and shared the prompt online as cleanyourtv. Within two days, thousands had repeated it on Xiaomi, TCL, Sony and Fire TV sets, and the project now claims testing on over 80 models.Another project, dumbtv by Muzzammil Yasin Sabuwala, targets ads, telemetry, Alexa and ACR, and has been tested on Sony, TCL, Philips, Hisense and Xiaomi TVs.Both work through Android Debug Bridge (ADB), a developer feature built into Android-based TVs, so nothing is rooted and changes can be reversed.Speed is part of the draw too. One X user said an afternoon with Claude Code disabled 25 bloat apps and replaced a 192MB stock launcher with an 83MB custom one.In India, where Google TV powers a large share of sets from Xiaomi, TCL, Sony and several budget brands, the pool of potential tinkerers is big.Results vary widely. One user said Claude bricked their Android TV, another got stuck midway through a Fire TV attempt, and an attempt on a Samsung set ended with a bricked TV too. Samsung's Tizen, LG's webOS, Roku and Amazon's newer Vega-based Fire TV Sticks are largely out of reach, and tampering can void the warranty on a new set.Toronto-based cybersecurity expert Ritesh Kotak warns that blocking services and skipping updates on a TV that stays online could leave it exposed to hackers, particularly as many sets now carry microphones. Vibe-coded scripts are also rarely built with security first, and may not be maintained for long.Safer routes exist. Turning off ACR and personalised ads in settings, using launchers like Projectivy or FLauncher, or keeping the TV offline with a streaming stick plugged in all reduce the clutter.The bigger reason behind the trend is fatigue. As tech analyst Carmi Levy puts it, people are "starting to get fed up" with devices that collect data at every turn.
Article Summary: Claude Code is being used to strip Android TV and Google TV sets back to the apps and HDMI inputs they paid for. Some users have bricked their sets, others have got stuck halfway, and security experts warn that cutting a connected TV off from updates could open the door to bigger problems. The bigger reason behind the trend is fatigue.

Article Title: $100 million data center equipment stolen as it becomes new target for cargo thieves in America; expert says: Easier to ...
Article Text:
Representative Image. Credit: X (Twitter)

“It’s like stealing pure gold bars,”

“We’ve seen some of these thefts go up into 30-plus million dollars for one particular shipment. It’s so much easier to steal this than to rob a bank.”

Two shipments disappeared after their security escorts were struck

“The accident was not an accident. The bad guys wanted that load, so they intentionally took out the escorts,”

How thieves are targeting data centre freight

Fewer theft incidents are producing larger losses

“The only way this works is if the drivers are not properly vetted,”

Data centre equipment is becoming a target for cargo thieves in the US. More than $100 million in freight has reportedly been stolen since June, according to industry executives, consultants, and investigators cited by NBC News. The losses come as the AI construction boom sends expensive servers, memory chips, cables and other equipment across American highways.said Keith Lewis, head of operations at risk-assessment firm Verisk CargoNet.NBC News identified nearly two dozen thefts involving high-end technology since last year, including incidents in California, Texas and Utah.In early June, a trailer carrying about $13 million in server equipment was travelling towards Fayetteville, Georgia, followed by two off-duty law enforcement officers in an unmarked car.While crossing the Mojave Desert, another vehicle struck the escort car, forcing it to stop. The trailer continued travelling and was found the next day at a truck yard in Stockton, California, with the equipment missing.said Gerardo Pachuca, a private investigator who previously investigated cargo theft for the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department.About three weeks later, a security vehicle escorting roughly $10 million in server rack components from San Jose to Texas was disabled in another collision.The trailer’s tracking app continued to show movement toward its destination, but investigators believe the location data was falsified. Neither shipment’s cargo has been recovered, according to the report.Investigators say organised groups increasingly use stolen trucking-company identities and compromised freight accounts to obtain valuable shipments. These methods let criminals identify cargo in advance and reroute legitimate pickups. Drivers collecting the goods may not know they are participating in a theft.Criminals can resell the equipment overseas or break it down for parts. Cargo experts told NBC News that buyers sometimes identify cargo before a shipment is stolen.In July, drivers using fake licences stole approximately $38 million in cables and cartridges in Reno, Nevada, according to people assisting the investigation. The goods were reportedly intended for shipment to Asia.Verisk CargoNet’s analysis found that overall cargo theft incidents fell 26% in the second quarter of 2026 compared with a year earlier. However, estimated losses more than doubled to $304.6 million, driven by several multimillion-dollar technology thefts.Security escorts are becoming more common as shipment values rise. Mike Duffy, co-founder and CEO of Solutions Group International, said his company escorts hundreds of loads each month, many connected to data centres.Scott Cornell, chair of supply-chain security organisation TAPA Americas, said checking drivers’ identities remains essential.he said.
Article Summary: Data centre equipment is becoming a target for cargo thieves in the US. More than $100 million in freight has reportedly been stolen since June. Losses come as the AI construction boom sends expensive servers, memory chips, cables and other equipment across American highways.

Article Title: Cybersecurity Awareness Month 2026: As AI takes centrestage, industry leaders say knowing basics is not enough to keep data safe online
Article Text:
Avaneesh Vats, vice president – Information Technology, Techno Digital:

As AI, cloud computing and automation become integral to India’s digital economy, cybersecurity must extend beyond protecting data and networks to securing the critical infrastructure that keeps essential services running. Data centres and power systems are increasingly interconnected through IT, operational technology (OT) and intelligent monitoring platforms.

However, their security priorities differ fundamentally.

While traditional IT security emphasises confidentiality, integrity and availability (CIA), OT environments prioritise availability, integrity and confidentiality (AIC), as operational continuity and safety are paramount. As these environments converge, vulnerabilities in one system can potentially affect critical operations and service continuity.

This Cybersecurity Awareness Month, the priority must shift from securing individual systems to building resilience across the entire infrastructure ecosystem. This calls for a secure-by-design approach, where cybersecurity is embedded into infrastructure architecture from the outset through network segmentation, continuous monitoring, secure access controls and tested incident response mechanisms.

As AI becomes increasingly integrated into critical operations, human oversight remains essential, particularly where automated decisions influence power and cooling systems. Ultimately, cyber resilience is not just about preventing attacks but about designing infrastructure that can withstand disruptions and sustain critical operations.

Mandy Andress, CISO, Elastic:

Each year, Cybersecurity Awareness Month brings the same reminders: use strong passwords, turn on MFA, and think before you click.

They still matter, but this year I keep coming back to one thought: AI isn’t just another item on the awareness list; it’s changing what security means. Models, API keys, and agent permissions are now high-value targets, and attackers noticed before most asset inventories did. Phishing emails no longer contain typos, and a voice call can sound exactly like your CFO.

We need to train people to verify the process, not just spot mistakes.

Agents are also a new kind of identity. When software can reason and act on its own, ‘who has access to what’ becomes much harder to answer. But defenders get leverage too, with AI compressing detection, investigation and response in ways I didn’t expect to see this soon. What hasn’t changed is that security is a team sport. AI governance can’t sit only with security; it needs legal, IT and the business at the same table, with shared ownership.

The organisations that come out ahead won’t be the ones that avoided disruption. They’ll be the ones that learned from it and became stronger because of it.

Dhananjay Ganjoo, Managing Director – India & SAARC, F5

AI is changing the very nature of enterprise risk because it is no longer operating in isolation. Across Indian organisations, AI models and autonomous agents are becoming part of business-critical operations, connecting to applications, accessing sensitive data and increasingly making decisions in real time. While this creates opportunities for innovation, it also opens new avenues for attackers through malicious prompts, API abuse and unauthorised data access. Critical vulnerabilities can be exploited and weaponised by bad actors at the speed of AI, and the only way to fight this is to introduce

AI-driven defense

.

We saw this threat escalate recently with PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), a pair of catastrophic, unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities that left defenders with zero lead time.

With details leaked on October 20 before patches were ready, attackers immediately began exploiting the flaw in the wild.

For sectors such as banking and healthcare, the response cannot be limited to detecting threats after they occur. Enterprises need greater visibility into how AI systems interact with sensitive information, stronger controls to identify unusual behaviour and the ability to stop malicious activity as it happens. These safeguards must work consistently across on-premises and cloud environments without disrupting critical services.

October is the Cybersecurity Awareness Month, and it gives companies, government bodies, schools and everyday users a chance to check how well they are protecting themselves in an increasingly connected world. But this year’s edition arrives at a very different point in the cybersecurity story. Industry leaders say 2026 comes at a completely different stage of cybersecurity development. While the basics have not changed, AI poses a greater risk and simply being aware of cyberthreats is no longer sufficient, because the threat landscape has changed drastically. Organisations now have to prepare for new kinds of attacks – that can operate at machine speed, that take advantage of flaws found by AI, that target interconnected digital ecosystems, and so on.
Article Summary: Cybersecurity must extend beyond protecting data and networks to securing the critical infrastructure that keeps essential services running. Data centres and power systems are increasingly interconnected through IT, operational technology (OT) and intelligent monitoring platforms. As these environments converge, vulnerabilities in one system can potentially affect service continuity.

Article Title: Two sons of doctors built Vera Health, a free medical AI tool; a year after reaching just a few thousand users, their 12-person startup says it serves 800,000 clinicians in 190 countries and has raise
Article Text:
How it works

Built for their fathers

How Vera Health differs from general AI tools

A year ago, Vera Health had a few thousand users. The company says it now serves more than 800,000 clinicians in 190 countries, and it has raised a $28.5 million Series A to keep growing. Threshold Ventures led the round, with participation from Mantis VC and SV Angel. Existing investors Y Combinator and Gradient also put in more money, bringing Vera’s total funding to $32 million. The company says it has done this with only 12 employees and little marketing. Most clinicians found the tool through colleagues, it says. Vera also says it has been the most downloaded clinical app in the world every month since June, and that in September it was downloaded more often than OpenEvidence and Doximity combined. Those figures come from Appark data cited by the company. Monthly downloads have more than tripled since February.Vera is strongest in Europe, according to company data. About one in four physicians in Spain and Italy use it, as do about one in seven in France. The company says daily active users already exceed the monthly active users it had when it raised the round, and that clinicians now ask it hundreds of thousands of questions a day.Vera is a clinical search engine. Its pitch is that it finds the evidence first and writes the answer afterward. It searches more than 60 million peer-reviewed papers, guidelines, consensus statements and drug labels. It ranks sources by study design, level of evidence, cohort size, recency, journal quality and citation impact. Each claim links to its source and is color-coded by the strength of the evidence behind it. For a rare condition with only a small case series, the answer shows up red, so doctors can see how little supports it.“Unlike other tools, we believe there’s value in making uncertainty visible,” co-founder Maxime Allouch said.The tool is free for licensed clinicians and trainees. The company says it does not train on their questions and is HIPAA and GDPR compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified. It has a partnership with the American College of Emergency Physicians, which puts the group’s clinical policies into answers with source attribution. Health systems can also load their own protocols through a feature called Vera Spaces.Allouch and Taieb Bennani, both MIT graduates and sons of physicians, founded Vera in 2024 at Y Combinator. They first built it for their own fathers. “Everyone on our team is a clinician, or the child or sibling of one,” Bennani said. He credited that background for the product’s spread among doctors.The company says the new money will go toward its evidence infrastructure, expansion into more markets, and partnerships with medical societies, publishers and health systems. Bennani said the mission is to “close the gap between what medicine knows and what every patient receives,” and that he wants the gap measured in seconds rather than years.Unlike general-purpose chatbots, Vera Health is built specifically for medical professionals and emphasises evidence-based responses. The platform searches more than 60 million peer-reviewed publications, clinical guidelines, consensus statements and drug labels before generating answers. Each claim is linked to supporting research and includes indications of the strength of the available evidence."Clinicians are the best data scientists I've ever met," said Taieb Bennani, co-founder of Vera Health. He added that many members of the company are either clinicians themselves or family members of healthcare professionals, helping shape the product around real-world clinical needs.Meanwhile, co-founder Maxime Allouch said the platform is designed to make uncertainty visible rather than presenting every response with equal confidence, a key distinction in medical decision-making.
Article Summary: Vera Health has raised a $28.5 million Series A to keep growing. Its pitch is that it finds the evidence first and writes the answer afterward. It searches more than 60 million peer-reviewed papers, guidelines, consensus statements and drug labels.

Article Title: FCC approves Amazon Leo's $11.5B acquisition of satellite operator Globalstar, setting up a new satellite connectivity battle with Elon Musk's SpaceX
Article Text:
FCC approves Amazon Leo's $11.5B acquisition of satellite operator Globalstar, setting up a new satellite connectivity battle with Elon Musk's Spacex

What FCC chairman said on Amazon Leo's $11.5B acquisition of Globalstar

What the approval means for Amazon Leo

The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has approved Amazon Leo’s $11.5 billion acquisition of Globalstar to “acquire approximately 25 megahertz of Globalstar’s internationally harmonized mobile-satellite service spectrum”. In a press release, the regulator said: “The companies’ complementary assets promise to enhance Amazon Leo’s entry into the direct-to-device segment and create a stronger satellite operator capable of offering fixed and mobile services to residential, business, and government customers”. The approval further strengthens the company’s satellite communications business as it prepares to challenge Elon Musk’s SpaceX.Amazon plans to use Globalstar’s mobile satellite spectrum and infrastructure to augment existing services with additional capacity and new capabilities, including broader connectivity beyond the reach of terrestrial wireless networks. The FCC said that it found the transaction “to benefit the public by enhancing data coverage in unserved or underserved areas, strengthening emergency communications capabilities, fostering growth in industrial and enterprise data services, and promoting more intensive use of mobile satellite service spectrum”.FCC Chairman Carr issued the following statement:“President Trump is restoring America’s technology leadership. And this FCC authorization is a significant step towards supercharging next-generation connectivity. By approving this deal, the FCC has empowered Amazon Leo to deliver fast, next-gen satellite broadband services, increase competition, and help communities stay connected all across the country.”The approval follows the Space Bureau’s decision last week to grant Globalstar’s request forU.S. market access for its non-geostationary C-3 System. The C-3 system is authorized to serve the U.S. market as part of a global network of 48 satellites arranged in 12 orbital planes, with four satellites per plane, operating at an inclination of 52 degrees and an altitude of 1,414 kilometers.The C-3 System may use 1610–1618.725 MHz for Earth-to-space mobile-satellite service links and 2483.5–2500 MHz for space-to-Earth service links. The authorization also covers feeder links and telemetry, tracking, and command operations in the 5091–5250 MHz Earth-to-space and 6875–7055 MHz space-to-Earth bands. Following the close of its transaction with Globalstar, Amazon Leo may use the C-3 System grant to build and launch this newly authorized system.Earlier this year, the Space Bureau granted SpaceX’s authorization to build, launch, and deploy a 15,000 satellite D2D constellation, as well as AST SpaceMobile’s authorization for a 248-satellite system.
Article Summary: The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has approved Amazon Leo’s $11.5 billion acquisition of satellite operator Globalstar. The approval further strengthens the company's satellite communications business as it prepares to challenge Elon Musk's SpaceX. Amazon plans to use the mobile satellite spectrum and infrastructure to augment existing services with additional capacity and new capabilities.

Article Title: After Oregon governor bans datacenters across the state over environmental permits; City council declares 'state of emergency'; warns residents: This will disrupt …
Article Text:
After Oregon governor bans datacenters across the state over environmental permits; City council declares 'state of emergency'; warns residents: This will disrupt …

Why Oregon city council declared emergency

Data centre restrictions put billions in investment at risk

What are Oregon’s restrictions on data centres

A city in Oregon has declared a state of emergency after the governor’s restrictions on new data centre projects threatened about $6 million in expected revenue. Umatilla officials warned that the move could delay public infrastructure projects, affect jobs and put billions of dollars in planned private investment at risk. The emergency declaration follows Oregon Governor Tina Kotek’s decision to suspend new environmental permits for data centres until July 2027. Umatilla officials say the restrictions could affect planned developments in the city, where data centres have become an important source of expected future revenue.Umatilla’s city council approved the emergency declaration over concerns that the state’s restrictions could disrupt its financial plans. The city had included expected data centre revenue in future budgets, with some of the money intended for infrastructure improvements.The projects at risk include a proposed police station and several million dollars in upgrades to the city’s water infrastructure. City Manager Dave Stockdale warned that delays in receiving the expected payments could force officials to reconsider the timelines for these projects.However, the city said it is not facing an immediate budget crisis. The money has not yet been received or spent, and existing public services and financial obligations remain unaffected.Umatilla currently has four operational data centres, while another facility is under construction and two more developments are awaiting completion. Companies operating in the area include Amazon Web Services and Sabey Data Centers. According to the city’s estimates, the restrictions could put more than $5 billion in planned private investment at risk. Officials also warned that at least 1,000 construction jobs, along with hundreds of permanent jobs and other employment opportunities, could be affected.Some projects awaiting regulatory approval could face delays of more than two years. Developers may also abandon their plans or move their investments to other locations, the city warned.“These consequences extend far beyond the interests of individual businesses. They threaten the broader economic and financial well-being of the Umatilla community,” said Dave Stockdale, Umatilla city manager.In October, Kotek directed Oregon’s environmental authorities to suspend new pollution permits for data centres, effectively restricting new development until July 2027. The governor had also halted transactions involving state-owned land intended for data centre projects while officials reviewed their potential long-term effects.The move followed an August decision to block the sale of 32 acres at Salem’s Mill Creek Corporate Center for a proposed Verrus development. Other local authorities have introduced restrictions as well. Hillsboro, for example, imposed a 120-day pause on new data centre developments in July 2026.Umatilla’s emergency resolution calls for the situation to be reviewed within 90 days. It also authorises an assessment of the possible financial and employment losses and urges the governor to reconsider the restrictions. Stockdale said the declaration was intended to protect future investment and infrastructure plans, rather than respond to an immediate shortage of operating funds.
Article Summary: Umatilla officials say the restrictions could affect planned developments in the city, where data centres have become an important source of expected future revenue. The city had included expected data centre revenue in future budgets, with some of the money intended for infrastructure improvements. The projects at risk include a proposed police station and several million dollars in upgrades to the city’s water infrastructure.

Article Title: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal shares an update on Temple device, writes ‘We are now taking pre-orders from everyone who signed up …’
Article Text:
Public pre-orders for Temple to begin from November 1

Temple's gradual rollout

What Temple does

Hand-made units, three-month delivery timeline

Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal has shared a fresh update on the rollout of the Temple wearable device, announcing that pre-orders have now opened for users who had signed up for early access over the past few months. n a post, he told those users to check their mailboxes for details. Everyone else, he said, should download the Temple app from the app stores, save their carts and get ready for general pre-orders on November 1. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Goyal said, “We are now taking pre-orders from everyone who signed up for early access over the last few months. Check your mailbox for more.”The entrepreneur also outlined plans for a wider rollout of the device. Users who have not registered for early access can download the Temple app from app stores, save products to their carts and prepare for public pre-orders beginning November 1. "Everyone else, download the @temple app from the app stores, save your carts and get ready for pre-orders on Nov 1," Goyal wrote in the post. The update suggests Temple is moving from its invite-only phase toward broader consumer availability, with the company now processing orders from its earliest sign-ups before opening sales to the public.The latest announcement follows earlier updates from Goyal indicating that Temple would adopt a measured launch strategy, with devices being produced and shipped in batches rather than through a mass-market rollout. Temple has attracted attention in India's startup ecosystem for its focus on tracking physiological and brain-related metrics. The wearable is designed to help users better understand factors such as recovery, stress, exercise and overall wellness through advanced sensing technology.Temple is an experimental health-tech wearable developed under a private initiative backed by Goyal. It uses optical sensors to track changes in cerebral blood flow, a metric the company calls BrainFlow. The device tracks blood flow and oxygenation inside the brain. The wearable first drew attention when Goyal appeared on a podcast in early 2026 wearing a small metallic clip-like device on his head.The latest update suggests that Temple's first production batch will be manufactured to order rather than mass-produced. Goyal said every unit will be hand-made, with deliveries expected within three months of purchase. The announcement gives potential buyers their first clear timeline for ordering the device, while also signalling that availability may remain limited during the initial phase as the company prioritises production quality over rapid expansion.It will come in six colours, with Real Jade, Deep Blue and Purple Funk marked as limited editions. Temple has not yet announced pricing, the number of devices in the first batch, or the exact date deliveries will begin, and said it would share more information before pre-orders open.
Article Summary: Public pre-orders for Temple to begin from November 1. Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal shared an update on the rollout of the Temple wearable device. He told those who signed up for early access to check their mailboxes for details. Goyal said every unit will be hand-made, with deliveries within three months.

Article Title: Oracle expands Nvidia AI chip deal, adds Google and other suppliers
Article Text:
Oracle expands Nvidia AI chip deal, adds Google and other suppliers

Oracle has expanded its cloud AI chip deal with Jensen Huang-led Nvidia while adding AI chips from other suppliers, including Google and Cerebras Systems, as it seeks to offer customers more options for running artificial intelligence workloads. Oracle and Nvidia said the cloud company would expand its use of Nvidia’s latest-generation Vera Rubin AI servers to "multi-gigawatt scale". “The expanded collaboration gives customers infrastructure for both the GPU-intensive work of training and serving frontier models and the CPU-intensive tasks agents perform between model calls, including executing tools, testing code and retrieving data. Customers can scale CPU and GPU resources independently to match their workloads, helping reduce idle capacity and put more of their infrastructure to productive use,” the company said in an announcement.Oracle is also changing parts of its AI infrastructure. It plans to use its own Acceleron networking chips in some Nvidia-based systems instead of certain Nvidia networking chips. The company will also begin offering Google’s tensor processing unit (TPU) chips for the first time."Different AI workloads have different compute needs," Mahesh Thiagarajan, president of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, said in a statement."That choice gives (customers) the flexibility to choose the right infrastructure for the performance, throughput and economics of each AI workload.”Beyond Google, Oracle plans to offer chips from SambaNova Systems and Cerebras Systems. Both companies make chips designed for AI inference, the process in which an AI system responds to user requests.While Nvidia leads the market for chips used to train AI systems, the inference market has a wider range of competitors. "That's a massive expansion of our customer base of tier-one customers," Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman said of the Oracle deal in an interview with Reuters. "We're being deployed in other people's data centers at large scale."
Article Summary: Oracle expands its cloud AI chip deal with Jensen Huang-led Nvidia. The company will also begin offering Google’s tensor processing unit (TPU) chips for the first time. Oracle plans to offer chips from SambaNova Systems and Cerebras Systems.
