Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan announced in late 2025 that they are shifting their donations, just weeks later Meta CEO gifted state of California $50 million to fund abatement, demolition and ...
Article Text:
Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan gave $50 million for Sacramento redevelopment

The philanthropic shift

California’s 5% tax on billionaires

Meta's AI ambitions

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan pledged a donation of $50 million to Sacramento State University. The gift from Zuckerberg and Chan was aimed to fund abatement, demolition and initial construction of a new downtown campus, Fortune reports. The donation came just weeks after the couple announced a major shift in the focus of the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI), directing most of its philanthropic efforts toward biomedical AI research and scientific discovery. The move signals a broader strategy that mirrors Zuckerberg's aggressive push into AI both at Meta and through the family's charitable ventures. California Governor Gavin Newsom announced the gift on January 28 and tied it to a redevelopment of three vacant state office buildings on Sacramento’s Capitol Mall. The money, from Zuckerberg and Meta, will make room for new student housing alongside academic space, including state-of-the-art STEM labs and an AI center.Zuckerberg also said that the investments will help strengthen communities and support the upcoming generation of leaders and innovators. Newsom added that this gift from the couple will enable the school keep building its pipeline of tech talent, and that students need to be able to afford to live where they study.Earlier this year, California Governor Gavin Newsom unveiled a $50 million gift from Zuckerberg and Meta tied to the redevelopment of three vacant state office buildings on Sacramento's Capitol Mall. As reported by Fortune, the funding made by Meta CEO and his wife will help support the abatement, demolition and initial construction work for a new downtown campus of Sacramento State University. The project is also said to include student housing, STEM-focused academic facilities along with a dedicated AI centre.Newsom further added that the investment would also lead to encourage the students for technology-related careers and will also take care of the housing needs at the same time. The donation made by Zuckerberg and Chan also comes at a time when California is debating over the proposed billionaire tax. The state is proposing to impose one-time 5% wealth tax on billionaires which has led to the exit of many high-profile and wealthy residents from the state. The report noted that Zuckerberg has not publicly commented on the proposal and continues to invest heavily in California through both business and philanthropic initiatives.The gift comes after Zuckerberg and his wife, Dr. Priscilla Chan, announced late last year that they would move most of the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI) toward AI-powered biomedical research. The initiative launched in 2015 with a pledge to give away 99 percent of the couple’s fortune. It has since moved away from its original focus on education and social justice, though the couple say they will continue to make other local donations.Biohub, a growing network of biomedical research institutes, is the centrepiece. The couple say it aims to cure or prevent all disease. At an event at the Biohub Imaging Institute in Redwood City in November, reported by the Associated Press, Zuckerberg said the Biohub model has been the most impactful thing they have done and that it will be the main focus of their philanthropy going forward.The refocus has had a cost. CZI recently laid off 70 staff, mostly at its Redwood City headquarters in San Mateo County. Fortune argues that the Sacramento AI center follows the same playbook, funding infrastructure for training AI talent, similar to Biohub’s shared research tools, rather than one-off scholarships or small, incremental gifts.The donation also arrives as California considers a one-time 5 percent tax on billionaires’ wealth. Fortune notes that several prominent billionaires, including Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, PayPal co-founder Peter Thiel and Craft Ventures’ David Sacks, have already moved their permanent residences out of state to avoid it. Zuckerberg has made no public statement about the tax and is instead putting more money into California. He owns a compound of 11 properties in Palo Alto’s Crescent Park neighbourhood, valued at more than $110 million, and Meta has a 57-acre headquarters campus nearby, plus more than 400,000 square feet of office space in Menlo Park.Fortune sees a common thread between Zuckerberg’s business and his giving. Meta has committed to spending between $115 billion and $135 billion on building “superintelligent” agents for feeds, ads and commerce, and the Sacramento gift helps build the talent pipeline for such jobs. Biohub, meanwhile, is focused on “frontier AI” and “frontier biology,” using large-scale models for virtual cells, immune reprogramming and disease prediction. In a November blog post, Zuckerberg and Chan wrote that they are very excited about the decade ahead and expect challenges as well as progress toward some of humanity’s long-term dreams.
Article Summary: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan pledged $50 million to Sacramento State University. The gift was aimed to fund abatement, demolition and initial construction of a new downtown campus. The donation comes just weeks after the couple announced a major shift in the focus of the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI) The move signals a broader strategy that mirrors Zuckerberg's aggressive push into AI.

Article Title: BlackBerry was once the phone everyone wanted, now company CEO says it is betting on AI robots
Article Text:
Blackberry moving beyond smartphone and cars

Expanding backlog and financial turnaround

Deepening integration with Nvidia

BlackBerry, the iconic brand whose physical-keyboard devices once dominated the early smartphone era, is putting its money into the growth of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered robots. Following years of operational restructuring, the Canadian technology company has evolved from a consumer mobile phone giant into an embedded software specialist. Now, as CEO John Giamatteo steers the enterprise past its automotive foundations, autonomous machines and “physical AI” seems to have taken center stage, as per a report by CNBC.BlackBerry’s core engine today is its QNX operating system. While best known for powering vehicle components ranging from electronic braking to semi-autonomous driving features, QNX is already running inside more than 275 million vehicles globally. However, executive leadership sees the next commercial frontier outside passenger cars.“While the products we sell today can’t be held in the palm of your hand, they’re pervasive around you. 275 million cars, robots, governments, medical instrumentation, supply chain. That’s the new BlackBerry, and that’s what’s driving all of our growth,” Giamatteo told CNBC.Unlike generative AI models that generate text, video or synthetic images, physical AI equips mechanical systems to perceive, navigate and safely interact with physical environments.Giamatteo noted that robotics has quickly become one of the fastest-growing segments inside the QNX portfolio. The company is leaning on decades of automotive safety certifications to position QNX as the foundational, mission-critical operating software that keeps commercial machines operating reliably.The pivot toward automated machinery is already feeding the company’s forward financial pipeline. According to the report, BlackBerry recently disclosed that its QNX royalty backlog crossed $1.2 billion, expanding by more than $250 million across two quarters. Giamatteo attributed that momentum to global automakers shifting toward sophisticated centralised computing architectures, an expanded portfolio of enterprise software solutions and accelerating customer demand for physical AI deployments.BlackBerry's stock has surged 142% just in 2026, a remarkable reversal of fortunes for a company that had been written off as dead after the emergence of touch screen rivals, including Apple's iPhone.Key to BlackBerry's robotics expansion is its technical relationship with chipmaker Nvidia. Originally established for automotive projects, the alliance has widened across industrial automation. Giamatteo confirmed that Nvidia has “standardised on QNX as the platform of choice” for its Halos Safety Stack.“That has opened up so many doors, an incredible pipeline of opportunity,” Giamatteo said. According to the CEO, that collaboration is directly driving QNX adoption across autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), robotic forklifts, and automated warehouse sleds ferrying pallet cargo to loading docks.
Article Summary: BlackBerry is putting its money into the growth of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered robots. CEO John Giamatteo steers the enterprise past its automotive foundations. The pivot toward automated machinery is already feeding the company’s forward financial pipeline.

Article Title: Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 employees months after 4,800 layoffs; staff have till December to decide; read HR head Amy Coleman's full memo to employees
Article Text:
After layoffs, Microsoft offers employees a buyout

Microsoft buyout eligibility depends on the team, not the employee

Microsoft's buyout can pay up to 39 weeks of salary but skips extended healthcare

This is Microsoft's second buyout of 2026, after months of layoffs

Microsoft says the buyouts are not a replacement for layoffs

A company spokesperson said the offer does not mean Microsoft needs fewer people, calling it one of several ways to adjust to changing business needs. Layoffs remain an option depending on business conditions. Like its Big Tech peers, Microsoft is under pressure to keep operating costs in check while it pours tens of billions of dollars into data centres and AI infrastructure.

There are no plans for another buyout right now, the spokesperson said, though an internal HR note says Microsoft may consider a future exit offer where there is a business and workforce need. In July, Coleman had said the company was studying whether voluntary exits could become a regular, possibly annual, fixture.

The first hint of what this round will cost may come on Wednesday, when Microsoft reports quarterly earnings.

As Coleman put it in her memo, "The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us. We'll learn from it."

Read Amy Coleman's full memo to Microsoft employees

Introducing a Voluntary Exit Offer

Today, we're introducing a new Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) to eligible employees within participating organizations. This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs.

The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we're evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter. This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program.

What employees should know

This offer will be available to eligible employees in participating teams in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States at level 70 and below.

This is a time-limited, voluntary program that gives those who are eligible the opportunity to leave Microsoft with financial support and career planning resources. Some organizations are providing the Voluntary Exit Offer, and some are not. Participation varies based on each business's priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs.

Eligible employees will receive an email with a link to their Voluntary Exit Offer details within the next few hours.

Looking ahead

The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us. We'll learn from it. At the same time, we'll keep helping people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft. There is no one-size-fits-all approach for every team or every employee. These are a few of the ways we're trying to meet different business needs while continuing to create opportunities for our own people to grow and contribute.

My promise is to continue to provide clarity, listen and learn and keep improving.

Thank you

Amy

Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its global workforce, and India is one of just four countries where the offer applies. Chief people officer Amy Coleman announced the Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) in a memo to staff on Monday, pitching it as a way for employees already weighing a future outside the company to leave now, with financial support and career planning help.The terms mirror Microsoft's standard severance. Eligible employees in the US, Canada, the UK and India at level 70 and below, a band that stretches up to general managers and some vice presidents, have until the first week of December to decide. Those who accept will exit at the end of the year. Unlike the retirement buyout Microsoft ran earlier this year, there is no age or tenure requirement, and performance plays no part.Not everyone at level 70 or below will get the email. Microsoft has left it to business leaders to decide whether their groups take part, and Coleman's memo says participation depends on each unit's priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs.Staff in AI experiences, Copilot, CoreAI, Windows + Devices, Xbox, finance and human resources are eligible, according to people familiar with the matter. Cloud + AI, Microsoft AI and the corporate, external and legal affairs group are participating partially.Sales, marketing, commercial business, discovery and quantum, and security teams are not part of the offer at all. Xbox, which took the biggest hit in July's layoffs, is back on the list.When Microsoft laid off US employees earlier this year, that severance meant at least 60 days of base pay while staying on the payroll, and for most people up to 39 weeks of base pay based on seniority and tenure. Employees at internal levels 64 and below got one week of base pay for every six months of service. Levels 65 to 67 got two weeks.The VEO also includes continued stock vesting, healthcare for a fixed period and career transition services. What it leaves out is the extended healthcare that drew long-serving staff to the spring retirement offer. Each eligible employee, including those in India, gets their individual terms by email.In spring, Microsoft ran its first-ever Voluntary Retirement Program for roughly 8,750 US employees at senior director level and below whose age plus years of service added up to at least 70. About 30% took it, and the company booked a $900 million charge for it in its April earnings report.Those exits shrank the layoffs that followed. Microsoft cut 4,800 jobs in July, about 2% of its workforce, with Xbox and commercial sales hit hardest, and let go of hundreds more in September. That came after more than 15,000 job cuts in 2025. Headcount stood at 223,000 on June 30, down from 228,000 a year earlier, and that figure predates the July cuts.This time, the company expects far fewer takers, since the offer is no longer aimed at people close to retirement.for everything you continue to do for our customers, Microsoft and for one another.
Article Summary: Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its global workforce. The terms mirror Microsoft's standard severance. Eligible employees in the US, Canada, the UK and India at level 70 and below have until the first week of December to decide. Those who accept will exit at the end of the year.

Article Title: Amazon updates AI usage rules for engineers, sends memo: We are seeing the beginning of AI’s effect on software engineering
Article Text:
Read full memo Amazon sent to engineers

Amazon engineering leaders have updated the role guidelines for Software Development Engineers (SDEs) to reflect that real-world results matter a lot more than specific tools. A company memo by Terk Terkowitz, vice president and distinguished engineer at Worldwide Amazon Stores, outlined leadership’s vision to move towards “Renaissance Developers” that combine human judgement and artificial intelligence, or AI. They urged engineers to integrate AI into their daily routines or risk being left behind, noting that AI will sit at the center of future engineering practices.Amazon cautioned against evaluating performance solely on “flawed” input metrics, such as the amount of tokens or lines of code, which could increase costs and complexity. Rather, leaders should look to the longer-term impacts on customers and businesses. Engineers were reminded that learning where AI falls short is “a finding, not a failing.” The memo also urged managers and individual contributors to keep their hands on AI tools but stay deeply connected to customer needs, ensuring tech adoption translates into tangible business results.An update from Amazon engineering leadership on the role of the developer in the age of AIAmazon engineering leaders revised the role guideline for software development engineers, underscoring what matters most is the outcome, not which tools are used.Written by Terk Terkowitz, VP/Distinguished Engineer, Worldwide Amazon StoresOne of the biggest shifts our leadership teams are seeing right now is how AI is changing the way software development engineers (SDEs) do their work, while balancing that the important elements of being an SDE are the same.Engineering leadership, including Distinguished and Senior Principal Engineers, from across Amazon recently came together to reaffirm what it means to be an SDE at Amazon. Based on key learnings and observations from the most successful SDEs at the company, they developed an updated role guideline. Our most prolific engineers have demonstrated that neither the developer role nor their output is defined by the use of AI. We're now in the era of the Renaissance Developer, blending AI tools with human judgment and domain expertise to build entirely new things. As a leader in agentic AI with thousands of SDEs, Amazon believes sharing our vision for the SDE role of the future can serve as a model for our customers.The following is a memo shared with software engineers across Amazon.-TerkDear SDEs and SDMs,As we developed the new version of the role guideline for Software Development Engineers (SDEs) at Amazon, we faced an important question: how much do we focus on AI? Historically we have tried to avoid having the SDE role guidelines be explicit about technology, reflecting the diversity of businesses that Amazon is in, and the work that our SDEs do. We have held to that approach as two decades of technology trends (the cloud, microservices, serverless, etc. ) have reshaped the work that SDEs do. In the Senior Principal and Distinguished Engineer communities, we have deeply debated whether this time is different. AI is changing the work of software engineering both more quickly and more fundamentally than these previous trends. What it means to be a software engineer, and what software engineering even is, is changing quickly and durably.Despite the speed of change, we believe that it is still early. We all need to embrace this change and take the time to learn, or we risk being left behind. We’re just seeing the beginning of AI’s effect on software engineering. While we have a vision for what the future looks like, there’s a lot that’s still emerging. We are certain that whatever future best practices are, AI will be at the center of software engineering practice. If you haven’t already, you should take the time to learn and apply AI into your daily work as soon as possible. If you’re already using AI, keep investing in finding better practice, and keep learning. The pace of change is high.It is difficult to define, in a way that will stand the test of time, what good AI powered engineering practices look like. Any definition we write now will likely look antiquated by this time next year. Antiquated definitions run the risk of slowing our progress, freezing our engineering practices in amber while the world moves on without us. To solve this problem, we have decided to focus on what is not changing as we evolved the SDE roles. Specifically, impact on our customers, our businesses, and our teams. The outcomes that matter aren’t changing, even if the inputs, tools, and techniques are changing faster than ever.“What’s going to change in the next five to ten years?” But I very rarely get asked “What’s not going to change in the next five to ten years?” That second question is actually the more important of the two.Jeff Bezos2012 interview with Werner VogelsThis conclusion made it easier to write the role guideline, but likely leaves you, our SDEs and SDMs, with an important question about how you should be using AI, and how you should be measuring AI usage in your teams and organizations. We believe that it is best to measure, and be measured by, long-term outcomes. But these outcomes can be time delayed, difficult to measure, and hard to isolate from other trends. In some cases, we have tackled those problems by using input metrics instead, like token usage or adoption of AI tools, or throughput metrics like code changes and reviews. We are all aware of how deeply flawed these metrics are, primarily because they are disconnected from what matters. We know that using these metrics could, if used as a target instead of a measure, drive negative outcomes, increasing costs (tokenmaxxing is at odds with frugality), and increasing complexity (measuring LOC is at odds with invent and simplify). We believe that this community, with your strong ownership and focus on delivering results, will help us avoid these negative outcomes.More positively, we have found that these input metrics correlate well with the outputs that matter and expect they will continue to do so for some time. This effect is driven both by increasing productivity and delivery on teams that have embraced AI the most (we call them frontier teams), and that teams and individuals who are not adopting AI or increasing output metrics are falling behind. Using these input metrics, with care and judgement, as you think about your career and your organization’s performance is appropriate. We recommend paying special attention to the 10th percentile (finding those teams who aren’t embracing AI effectively and understanding why) and the 90th percentile (finding those teams who are heavily using AI and understanding whether they’re seeing delivery increases to match) of AI adoption. Working together, over time, we will find better metrics and set smarter goals.“Good inventors and designers deeply understand their customer. They spend tremendous energy developing that intuition. They study and understand many anecdotes rather than only the averages you’ll find on surveys.”Jeff Bezos2016 Letter to ShareholdersTo paraphrase: Good leaders deeply understand their team's work. They spend tremendous energy developing that intuition. They study and understand many anecdotes, and carefully track outputs, rather than only surface-level metrics.If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing. Document why, share it with your community of peers, bring it to your manager, and work to find solutions. An engineer who can explain where AI does not yet help their work is demonstrating the judgement we are asking for.As a technical or organizational leader, part of your job is making sure that your team or organization is using AI to the best effect to improve delivery for customers and your business. That requires deeply understanding these technologies yourself, working with them hands-on rather than relying on what you hear, and understanding how others are using them. Sufficient understanding means you have used these tools on your production work, can describe a task where they helped and a task where they did not, and can explain that judgement to your team. Deploying AI in your organizations requires carefully balancing between exploring new and better ways to do things and investing in doubling down on the ones you already have. Judgement and care are key. As a leader, we expect you to be taking ownership of connecting the inputs and outputs in your team or organization.As we have looked across our organizations, we have found that the leaders who are having the most impact are those doubling down on learn and be curious. Both spending the time they need to learn AI and making time for the people they lead to do the same. We have seen that the returns on this investment in our organizations are disproportionately large, with teams who have followed their curiosity (appropriately balanced with deliver results and insist on the highest standards) seeing the most positive impact from AI adoption.We have also found that SDEs and SDMs who are closer to their products and businesses are able to take the most advantage of AI and agentic software development. As Amazon has grown, we’ve seen some of our ICs and SDMs become less connected to their customers and business. We want to reverse this trend. We recommend that ICs of all levels find ways to become deeply connected to your customers, and your team or org’s product direction. As always, the scope and depth of this ownership will increase as you become more senior. For SDMs, we also recommend spending time making sure you’re close to your customers and business, and you’re helping the ICs in your organization to do the same.This is a time of change for our industry, and a time of change for what it means to be a software engineer. We believe that the opportunity for software, and for software engineers, has never been larger. We’re more excited about the future of software development, and of our role as engineers, than ever before. Partnering with you as strong, curious, customer-obsessed owners, we will invent the future of software development together.We will continue to evolve the SDE role over the coming years, as AI’s effect on our business and engineering practices becomes clear. But we believe that’s unlikely to change what really matters: obsession with our customers, and a long-term focus on delivering results.
Article Summary: Amazon engineering leaders have updated the role guidelines for Software Development Engineers (SDEs) They urge engineers to integrate AI into their daily routines or risk being left behind. Amazon cautioned against evaluating performance solely on “flawed” input metrics.

Article Title: Upset Palmer Luckey is not leaving California over 'Billionaire tax', making it very clear that he will stay, as wants to ...
Article Text:
Palmer Luckey, founder of Oculus and Anduril Industries.

Why Palmer Luckey is against the proposed Wealth tax

Palmer Luckey is not joining billionaires leaving or planning to leave California over the proposed billionaire wealth tax. Founder of Anduril Industries, one of America's biggest defence technology companies, has made it clear that he is very much staying in the state, Wealth Tax or no Wealth Tax. Speaking at an invite-only press conference, the 34-year-old founder made it clear that while he opposes the contentious ballot initiative, he has no intention of packing his bags. His remarks first appeared in TechCrunch.“I think that this tax act, if you can call it a tax, is going to cause a lot of problems. It’s causing a lot of people to run who I don’t want to be running,” Luckey said. “As of right now, though, I’m not running. I am staying. I think California is something special. I want to fight for California.”Luckey, who grew up in Long Beach, entered California's ultra-wealthy tier at age 21 after selling his Virtual Reality company Oculus VR to Facebook for $2 billion in 2014. His current venture, defense technology company Anduril, is headquartered in Costa Mesa. Anduril was recently valued at $61 billion.Despite concerns that partner companies and peer executives are reconsidering their California footprint, Luckey signaled that his fight will likely move to the courts if voters approve the measure.“I’m planning on staying in California. I’m going to keep fighting it,” Luckey said. “I’m hoping that this doesn’t pass. I’m hoping if it does pass, that there are legal challenges.”Luckey criticized the backing behind the measure, pointing to its primary sponsor, an affiliate of the United Healthcare Workers union, alleging the group is seeking revenue "for their uses." Proponents of the initiative maintain that the generated funds are earmarked for vital public services, including education, food assistance, and Medi-Cal, the state’s healthcare program for low-income residents.The proposed ballot measure seeks to levy an annual tax on the net worth of California’s wealthiest residents. Luckey also said he was concerned that the proposed wealth tax could penalize tech leaders with super-voting shares, which founders often use to retain control of their companies after raising money. Luckey said that the possibility of taxing voting shares was the “real problem” with the tax.“That is not a tax on ownership. It is a tax on control,” Luckey said, calling the mechanism “truly unprecedented” and warning that it effectively amounts to a “post facto seize [of] people’s past and future wealth.”As per Forbes estimates, Luckey’s net worth stands at $5.9 billion. During the press conference, Luckey estimated he could owe up to 5%, or $3 billion, based on his super-voting shares in the company.
Article Summary: Palmer Luckey, founder of Oculus VR and Anduril Industries, says he is staying in California. Luckey is against the proposed Wealth tax on the state's wealthiest residents. The 34-year-old is concerned that the tax could penalize tech leaders with super-voting shares.

Article Title: Google DeepMind launches Genie 4, CEO Sundar Pichai calls it ‘our most realistic and interactive world model’
Article Text:
Excited to share Genie 4 today our most realistic and interactive world model:

- steer dynamic environments in real time, shaping events, camera angles, and actions

- generate native audio matched to the world, from realistic background sounds to characters who can converse in real time!

- simulate photorealistic scenes and real-world physics

- create more coherent multi-step events through reasoning from Gemini

We've started to roll out as a research preview to trusted testers.

Coming soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners via the Gemini API and AI Studio.

Genie 4 is built on Gemini Intelligence

Google lists four core breakthroughs in Genie 4

Real-time scene direction

Advanced physics and motion

Native audio generation

Complex multi-step simulation

Google DeepMind has officially unveiled Genie 4, its world artificial intelligence (AI) model that introduces real-time, interactive world simulation with native audio and realism. The system allows users to generate and actively navigate dynamic environments, steering scenes on the fly while the model simultaneously calculates physics, character behavior, and soundscapes. Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai highlighted the milestone, calling Genie 4 “our most realistic and interactive world model.”Genie 4 is not a standalone graphics engine; it directly integrates the multimodal reasoning capabilities of Google’s Gemini family:Gemini Omni: Anchors each simulation in authentic real-world appearances, physical dynamics and visual continuity.Gemini reasoning models: Maintain scene logic, ensuring events unfold with cause-and-effect coherence over time.Gemini 3.8 Flash: Operates as an active agent in the loop. As Genie 4 renders the world, Gemini 3.8 Flash tracks incoming frames, breaks broad goals into sequential steps, verifies that actions succeed, and adapts plans instantly whenever the scene shifts or a user intervenes.Google DeepMind detailed four primary technical advancements that define the new world model:Users can explore simulated environments using standard keyboard controls for navigation and camera positioning, while using plain text prompts to alter the world in real time. They can change the weather, adjust camera angles, or introduce new characters and objects.Google says that Genie 4 delivers a significant leap in physical accuracy, accurately rendering complex interactions such as aerodynamics, collisions, and environmental resistance. Character animation sees an equally sharp upgrade: digital figures move naturally, interact organically with their surroundings, and respond immediately to real-time steering.As the first real-time world model to generate synchronised audio natively, Genie 4 produces sound directly alongside visual frames, Google says. This includes contextual ambient soundscapes, such as wind through trees or breaking ocean waves as well as background music.Crucially, the model handles interactive, real-time spoken dialogue. Characters converse, react, and respond on the fly to user prompts and unfolding environmental events.By pairing world generation with advanced AI reasoning, Genie 4 can simulate multi-stage events, allowing developers to see how artificial agents navigate complex settings before deploying them into real-world scenarios.
Article Summary: Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4, its world artificial intelligence (AI) model. System introduces real-time, interactive world simulation with native audio and realism. System allows users to generate and actively navigate dynamic environments, steering scenes on the fly. Model simultaneously calculates physics, character behavior, and soundscapes.

Article Title: Digi Yatra to start international passenger trials at seven airports on November 1, plans wider rollout in 2027: What it means for users
Article Text:
Representative Image

Digi Yatra international trials: Who can use it and how it works

"Digi Yatra has demonstrated how digital identity can simplify domestic air travel.

With the start of international passenger trials, we are taking an important step towards extending this experience to eligible Indian nationals travelling internationally."

Digi Yatra app gets a redesigned interface

Digi Yatra plans wider rollout in 2027

Digi Yatra is opening international passenger trials. Starting November 1, eligible Indian nationals with e-passports travelling on Air India and IndiGo can use digital identity credentials at selected airport checkpoints. The trials cover seven airports and will run through December 2026, with passenger feedback informing plans for a wider rollout in 2027. The service will initially be available to passengers travelling on international flights operated by Air India and IndiGo, subject to airport infrastructure availability.The trials will cover Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Cochin, Mumbai, Chennai and Amritsar airports. Eligible passengers can use Digi Yatra for terminal entry, security hold areas, and boarding gates at enabled touchpoints. While the trial covers all international destinations served by Air India, IndiGo passengers will be eligible on select international routes.The international passenger trial is limited to Indian nationals holding e-passports and travelling on eligible international flights operated by Air India and IndiGo.Passengers must create an e-passport-based Verifiable Credential (VC) through the Digi Yatra app before using the service.Passengers do this by scanning the machine-readable zone (MRZ) of the e-passport, reading the embedded chip using a compatible smartphone's Near Field Communication (NFC) capability, taking a selfie, and verifying the details. Once created, the digital credential will be stored in the passenger’s Digi Yatra wallet on the passenger’s device and can be used at enabled airport touchpoints during the trial.However, Digi Yatra will not replace the existing international travel process. Passengers will still need to carry their travel documents and complete mandatory airline document checks, immigration and other travel formalities as usual. Service availability will also depend on each airport's infrastructure.Suresh Khadakbhavi, CEO of Digi Yatra Foundation, said,He added that interoperability with global frameworks such as the International Air Transport Association's (IATA) One ID and the International Civil Aviation Organization's (ICAO) Public Key Directory (PKD) would be key to exploring how e-passport-based digital credentials could enable more seamless, secure journeys across borders.Alongside the international passenger trials, Digi Yatra has introduced a redesigned mobile app to simplify navigation and make the digital identity process clearer for users.The update brings a cleaner interface, an improved boarding pass display with airline-mapped colours, more intuitive navigation and a more structured credential wallet. It also adds clearer indicators for guardian and minor credentials and a redesigned consent screen.The updated consent screen is intended to help passengers understand what information is being shared, with whom and for what purpose. Digi Yatra said the changes aim to improve clarity, accessibility and the overall user experience, while keeping passenger consent, privacy and security central to the platform.Digi Yatra currently has more than 26.5 million users and has enabled over 110 million journeys, according to the company. The platform operates across 39 domestic airports and serves 11 domestic airlines, with average airport adoption at about 30%.The company also plans to expand the app's language support. It is currently available in 11 regional languages and plans to support all 22 scheduled by 2027. The company also plans to cover another 25 domestic airports by the same year.The international passenger trials will give Digi Yatra an opportunity to assess how its digital identity system works for eligible travellers beyond domestic air travel. Feedback from the three-month programme will help inform plans for a wider rollout in 2027, while the redesigned app aims to improve the experience for existing users.
Article Summary: Digi Yatra is opening international passenger trials. Eligible Indian nationals with e-passports travelling on Air India and IndiGo can use digital identity credentials. The trials cover seven airports and will run through December 2026, with passenger feedback informing plans for a wider rollout in 2027.

Article Title: As Intel works to reclaim chip leadership, CEO Lip-Bu Tan hints at fresh areas of partnership with AMD
Article Text:
Lip-Bu Tan, CEO of Intel

Expanding beyond traditional processors

Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan has reportedly discussed potential opportunities for collaboration with AMD chief Lisa Su. Tan confirmed the partnership, according to a recording of Tan’s October 24 fireside chat with Chinese American Semiconductor Professional Association (CASPA) President Jimmy Cheng but he did not elaborate on the exact areas of cooperation discussed with Su. Notably, Intel and AMD have joined forces whenever their commercial interests align.During the CASPA conversation, Tan outlined an aggressive turnaround strategy centered on reviving Intel's core central processing unit (CPU) division, creating specialised silicon tailored to client workloads, and bringing outside business to its manufacturing foundries, as per a report by Tom’s Hardware.Historically, Intel anchored its business model around rigid, internal product roadmaps. Tan argued that the enterprise must become far more adaptable as clients increasingly demand custom chips built for specialised computational tasks. He cited Intel’s flagship Xeon lineup as a prime example of where this mindset is shifting, running parallel to ongoing work on GPUs and dedicated accelerators.“We have to reclaim the leadership in CPU. That is something that I am very determined to do. Intel is so proud they never want to modify for customer needs.I'm modifying it for customer needs, and so that, I think, to me, is a fast-growing area, and I'm double, triple down on it,” Tan said.The push for custom silicon extends well past standard computer processors. Tan pointed to several emerging technologies as major long-term revenue drivers, which include, application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), co-packaged optics (CPO), physical artificial intelligence (AI) and advanced packaging solutions.Tan set an ambitious target for these emerging segments, stating he expects two or three of them to eventually generate roughly 10% of Intel’s total revenue each.Intel’s contract manufacturing business, Intel Foundry, serves as the other core pillar in Tan’s restructuring roadmap. Winning external chip design customers remains essential to making those massive manufacturing investments pay off.On the fabrication front, Tan said that Intel’s 18A manufacturing node has officially reached volume production. Meanwhile, work on the subsequent 14A process is advancing steadily. To support third-party adoption, Intel has already distributed version 0.5 of its 14A process design kit (PDK), supplying prospective clients with the technical documentation, design rules, and tools required to build chips on the upcoming node.
Article Summary: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan has reportedly discussed potential opportunities for collaboration with AMD chief Lisa Su. Tan confirmed the partnership, according to a recording of Tan’s October 24 fireside chat with Chinese American Semiconductor Professional Association (CASPA) President Jimmy Cheng.

Article Title: Scale AI’s Outlier has more than 900,000 freelancers; a privacy group alleges up to 19 trackers monitor workers and is asking European regulators to fine the company
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation

What do the complaints allege about worker tracking

“You don't work when you want,

“You work when the platform wants you to and there are tasks available.”

Why are Scale AI’s identity checks being challenged

Scale AI’s Outlier faces complaints over alleged monitoring of freelancers. According to a report by the news agency Reuters, European digital privacy advocacy group noyb has filed five complaints in France, Italy, the Netherlands and Austria against the company founded by Meta’s current chief AI officer and highest-paid employee, Alexandr Wang. The complaints allege that the platform illegally tracks people who produce training data for artificial intelligence (AI)models. According to the Reuters report, the complaints say up to 19 trackers monitor workers, including by recording keystrokes and mouse movements every few seconds.Outlier has more than 900,000 freelancers performing tasks for clients such as Meta, OpenAI and Google. Noyb is asking European regulators to fine Scale AI and examine how the platform assigns work. The complaints also challenge its identity checks and how it handles workers’ requests for their personal data.The complaints, which Reuters reviewed, describe monitoring that records workers’ activity throughout their tasks. An investigation by Paris-based research collective DiPLab found that the resulting data file could be reconstructed into a video replaying a work session from beginning to end.Thomas Le Bonniec, who spent two years studying Outlier for DiPLab, also questioned how much control freelancers have over their schedules.” Le Bonniec said.Noyb’s request that regulators examine task allocation raises concerns about how the platform decides which work is available to freelancers.Workers must submit identification documents and a facial video to Persona, an identity verification company. The complaints allege that these checks were invasive, repeated without explanation, and breached European Union rules governing biometric data, which can identify people through physical characteristics. However, these are mere allegations in the complaints, not findings announced by regulators.DiPLab’s investigation also identified game-like mechanisms that encouraged workers to complete tasks, with bonuses as a key part of the incentive system. Citing worker interviews, Le Bonniec said Outlier offered bonuses of $100 to $200 for completing 200 tasks within 24 hours.He pointed to a 2021 fine Italy’s data protection authority imposed on delivery platform Glovo for similar gamification practices, in which rewards or targets are used to influence workers’ behaviour.Separately, four workers requested copies of their personal data from Outlier between December 2025 and May 2026. According to the complaints, none received an answer.
Article Summary: Scale AI’s Outlier faces complaints over alleged monitoring of freelancers. European digital privacy advocacy group noyb has filed five complaints against the company. The complaints allege that the platform illegally tracks people who produce training data for artificial intelligence (AI)models.

Article Title: Comcast co-founder Julian Brodsky and wife Lois give $20 million to expand the Philadelphia Museum of Art's learning space from 5,901 to about 19,000 sq ft, helping it welcome more than 36,000 student
Article Text:
Image credit: Philadelphia Museum of Art (PMA)​

What will the new learning centre include

“It will address the museum’s need for expanded capacity to host school groups, while providing dedicated spaces for programming and studios for hands-on learning.”

Why are the Brodskys supporting the project

“Lois and I are incredibly happy to support the new Learning and Engagement Center,”

“It comes at a wonderful moment, bringing together so many of the initiatives we are passionate about and reflecting our deep love for the Philadelphia Museum of Art. Throughout our lives, we have been ardently involved in educational initiatives, with a particular focus on children and families from underserved communities.”

Which students can visit for free

Comcast co-founder Julian Brodsky and wife Lois are funding a museum expansion. Their $20 million gift to the Philadelphia Museum of Art will establish a learning and engagement centre in its north wing. The recently announced project will expand dedicated education space from 5,901 square feet to approximately 19,000 square feet, according to preliminary plans reported by The Philadelphia Inquirer.The museum currently welcomes approximately 36,000 students annually and expects the centre to increase its capacity. Named the Lois G. and Julian A. Brodsky Learning and Engagement Center, it will include spaces for school groups, children, families and visitors of all ages. The museum expects designs by summer 2027, with construction anticipated to finish within a few years.Initial plans include a family learning centre, art studios, a visitor orientation area and a multipurpose community hub. The museum is working with Philadelphia-based architecture firm MGA Partners on the design, according to its announcement.The expansion will retain existing education rooms while converting areas currently used part-time for educational activities into dedicated learning spaces, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported.Audrey Hudson, the museum’s deputy director for learning and engagement, said the project would provide more room for school visits and practical activities.The centre will be the museum’s first major building project since the Core Project, Frank Gehry’s four-year interior renovation and expansion, which reopened to the public in May 2021.The couple has supported the museum for decades through donations, volunteering, and board service.Julian Brodsky said.Julian, one of Comcast's three founding principals, joined the museum's board in 1995 and became a trustee emeritus in 2024. Lois began volunteering in 1982 and led visitors through its collections and exhibitions from 1986 to 2019.Their earlier contributions included support recognised through the naming of the Lois Green Brodsky Gallery in 2005 and funding for the Brodsky Curator of Photographs position in 2009.The museum provides free guided school visits and bus transportation for eligible groups. These include School District of Philadelphia students, district preschools and Head Start programs, Philadelphia Parks & Recreation camps, and Title I schools serving children from low-income families throughout the tri-state region and Delaware Valley. General admission is also free for visitors aged 18 and younger.
Article Summary: Comcast co-founder Julian Brodsky and wife Lois are funding a museum expansion. Their $20 million gift to the Philadelphia Museum of Art will establish a learning and engagement centre in its north wing. The centre will include spaces for school groups, children, families and visitors of all ages. The museum currently welcomes approximately 36,000 students annually.

Article Title: In 2025, Apple invested in California’s 14,000-acre Gualala River Forest, expanding its Restore Fund amid warnings that 13 million acres of US forests could disappear by 2050
Article Text:
PC: AP

How Apple and The Conservation Fund plan to protect California’s redwood forests

Why 13 million acres are at risk by 2050

The Restore Fund has expanded beyond its original projects

How Apple’s Gualala River Forest project supports its 2030 carbon neutrality goal

Conservation work extends to communities around the world

California’s coastal redwoods can live for centuries, growing in forests that support wildlife, store carbon and provide work for nearby communities. Yet some of these landscapes remain vulnerable to logging pressures and changes in how the land is managed. In September 2025, Apple announced an investment in the long-term protection and restoration of 14,000 acres of redwood forest in Mendocino County, part of a wider effort to fund nature-based carbon removal. The announcement came against a warning from The Conservation Fund that 13 million acres of American forests were at risk of disappearing by 2050, as reported by Apple Newsroom. The partnership also reflects how technology companies are increasingly financing conservation beyond their own operations.The project centres on the Gualala River Forest in northern California, an area of coastal redwoods that also contains sugar pines and California black oaks. The forest provides habitat for hundreds of wildlife species, while its timber and associated activities contribute to the economies of communities along the northern coast.Apple is working with The Conservation Fund, a US non-profit organisation that acquires threatened landscapes and forests to protect them from degradation.Under the arrangement, the organisation will continue managing the property with an emphasis on sustainable forestry and long-term restoration. Apple, in return, will receive carbon credits generated as the forest grows and stores carbon over time. Sustainable management of a working forest involves maintaining its ecological value while allowing appropriate economic activity to continue. The partnership is intended to protect the landscape over the long term, rather than treating the purchase of carbon credits as a substitute for managing the forest itself.The Conservation Fund has been protecting forestland in California's redwood region since 2004, safeguarding more than 120,000 acres across the state during that period. Its existing work with Apple also includes the protection of more than 36,000 acres of working forest in Maine and North Carolina.The scale of the wider threat was highlighted by Larry Selzer, president and chief executive of The Conservation Fund said, “America’s forests are under immense pressure, with 13 million acres at risk of vanishing by 2050. This is one of the defining conservation challenges of our time.”Forest loss and degradation can affect wildlife habitats, carbon storage and the industries that depend on healthy woodland. In rural areas, forests are also tied to employment, from timber production to activities supporting local businesses. Selzer said American forests supported more than two million jobs.Protecting a working forest presents a different challenge from conserving land where commercial activity is prohibited. The aim is to maintain the landscape's ecological functions while managing the resources it provides. That requires long-term planning, monitoring and decisions about how the forest is used.For Apple and The Conservation Fund, the California partnership offers one way to address those competing demands. Its contribution will be measured over time through the forest's continued growth, its management and the carbon credits generated by the project.The California investment forms part of Apple's Restore Fund, launched in 2021 with Goldman Sachs and Conservation International. The initiative was established to encourage investment in nature-based carbon removal, using forests and other ecosystems to draw carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.Apple expanded the programme in 2023 with a fund managed by Climate Asset Management. In 2025, it added direct investments in nature-based projects in the United States and Latin America. By the time of the redwood announcement, the initiative had investments in two dozen conservation and regenerative agriculture projects across six continents. Suppliers TSMC and Murata had also invested in the fund.The projects vary by location and purpose. Some focus on protecting existing natural landscapes, while others involve regenerative agriculture or restoring ecosystems capable of storing carbon. The broader approach gives Apple a way to support projects outside its immediate supply chain, although each investment depends on the conditions of the particular landscape and the work carried out there.Apple's environmental investments are linked to its goal of becoming carbon neutral across its entire business footprint by the end of 2030. The company has said it aims to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions by 75% compared with 2015 levels, with carbon removal intended to address the remaining emissions. According to Apple, it had already reduced its emissions by more than 60% against that baseline by the time of the 2025 announcement. The company and its suppliers were aiming to remove 9.6 million metric tonnes of carbon from the atmosphere each year by 2030 through projects around the world.Forests are central to this approach because trees absorb carbon dioxide as they grow and retain carbon in their biomass. Measuring that storage, however, requires more than counting trees. The Conservation Fund monitors selected trees in the Gualala River Forest by recording their height and diameter repeatedly, allowing changes in growth to be tracked over time.Those measurements help establish how much carbon is being stored in the forest. They also provide a basis for monitoring the results of management and restoration activities. For a project that generates carbon credits, the ability to measure and verify carbon storage is an important part of demonstrating its environmental contribution.Apple's work on forests is part of a wider programme of environmental funding. Alongside Restore Fund investments, the company announced grants for conservation organisations and community initiatives in September 2025.Some of that funding was directed towards Conservation International's efforts to develop conservation leadership and strengthen local capacity to protect ecosystems, including mangrove forests in India. Apple also announced further support for the Jane Goodall Institute's global Roots and Shoots programme, which involves community-led environmental and conservation activities.A separate project with The Nature Conservancy was intended to assess the quality of remote-sensing tools used to monitor and verify natural climate solutions. Such tools can help track environmental changes across large or difficult-to-access landscapes, though their reliability needs to be evaluated if they are to support credible measurements of project outcomes.
Article Summary: Apple is investing in the long-term protection and restoration of 14,000 acres of redwood forest in Mendocino County, California. The company will receive carbon credits generated as the forest grows and stores carbon over time. The Conservation Fund has been protecting forestland in California's redwood region since 2004.

Article Title: More than 2.1 million US customers of cash-advance app Cleo AI are set to receive a share of $15.8 million as federal refunds begin on October 27, following allegations of hidden fees and misleading f
Article Text:
FTC alleged consumers were misled

How to get a payment

No need for consumers to file claims

Company settled but denied wrongdoing

More than 2.1 million customers of cash-advance app Cleo AI are set to receive refunds from the US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) beginning October 27, after regulators accused the company of misleading users about how much money they could borrow, how quickly funds would arrive, and how easy it was to cancel subscriptions. The FTC said it is returning more than $15.8 million to 2,124,796 consumers who paid for eligible instant cash advances through the app. The refunds stem from a $17 million settlement reached in 2025 following a lawsuit filed by the agency against Cleo AI. Payments will be distributed through PayPal starting October 27.The refunds stem from a complaint the FTC filed in March 2025. It alleged that Cleo AI misled consumers with promises of fast money, advertising access to “hundreds of dollars” in cash advances when almost no one received anything close to the advertised amounts. The agency also alleged that the company charged hidden fees for same-day or instant cash advances that often did not arrive until the next day, and that it made cancelling subscriptions difficult. The FTC’s announcement refers to the case in connection with a $17 million payment by the company that settled the lawsuit, and the refunds come from that money.Eligible consumers do not need to apply. The refund administrator, Rust Consulting, Inc.,is handling the process and can be reached at 877-788-4958 for questions about a payment. The FTC also points consumers to the frequently asked questions on its refund programme page. The agency stressed that it never requires people to pay money or provide account information to receive a payment, so anyone who is asked to do either should be wary. The FTC says it will never demand money, make threats, tell you to transfer money or promise you a prize, and consumers can report suspected scams at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.The FTC said eligible customers have been identified using company records and do not need to submit a claim to receive a refund. Consumers eligible for payment are being notified via email between October 8 and October 26, with PayPal payments beginning October 27. Recipients will have 30 days to accept the payment once it is issued. The agency noted that simply downloading the app or subscribing to a service does not automatically qualify a person for compensation. Only customers who paid for eligible instant cash advances are included in the refund programme.The refund programme follows a settlement agreement under which Cleo AI agreed to pay $17 million. According to reports, the company did not admit wrongdoing as part of the settlement. The firm's general counsel previously said the FTC's claims were inaccurate and reflected a misunderstanding of the business.
Article Summary: FTC says it is returning more than $15.8 million to 2,124,796 consumers who paid for eligible instant cash advances through the app. The refunds stem from a $17 million settlement reached in 2025 following a lawsuit filed by the agency against Cleo AI. Payments will be distributed through PayPal starting October 27.

Article Title: Nvidia commits $3 billion to Meta's new share offering and expands work on Zuckerberg's Muse AI assistant, which can connect to users' email and calendar apps, as the two tech giants deepen their part
Article Text:
Meta-Nvidia to mark deeper alliance on ‘Muse

Inside Meta’s record capital plan

Nvidia is reportedly putting $3 billion into Meta’s equity offering, anchoring a wider agreement between the two tech giants to jointly develop Meta’s “Muse” artificial intelligence (AI) assistant and refine the software running behind it. As per a report by news agency Reuters, the investment forms part of an enormous capital drive by Meta, which raised the target for its latest equity offering on Tuesday to $97.5 billion, which is the biggest fundraising campaign in the company’s history. Notably, the capital influx is set to fund Meta’s AI infrastructure buildup even as it pours billions into specialised data centre campuses and advanced chips to stay competitive with rival AI developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic.Beyond the financial backing, Tuesday’s (October 27) agreement ties Nvidia’s hardware closer to Meta’s software ecosystem. Meta’s Muse models and autonomous agents already operate on Nvidia infrastructure but with the new collaboration aims to boost performance and control computing expenses.Referred to internally as “Hatch,” Muse serves as the focal point for CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s vision of bringing “personal superintelligence” to the billions of daily active users across Meta's apps.The assistant is modeled on the open-source agent framework OpenClaw and is built to integrate deeply into everyday digital routines.Looking ahead, Meta and Nvidia noted they may also look into expanding collaboration around Nvidia’s OpenShell framework. This effort could include deploying software in secure environments and utilizing a specialised tool called “Sentry” to track and monitor the behavior of autonomous AI agents.The massive $97.5 billion target represents an upward revision, when Meta first unveiled blueprints to raise up to $95 billion while keeping Zuckerberg's majority voting control intact. As originally outlined, the financing package is split across two core mechanisms – roughly $35 billion issued in common and preferred stock, and a separate share sale program valued at up to $60 billion.Meta said the larger, $60 billion leg will roll out only after its newly established, non-voting Class C shares begin trading publicly, which is expected to occur in the first quarter of 2027.Nvidia’s $3 billion commitment highlights intense interest from Meta's core hardware vendors. Key semiconductor partners, including Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Broadcom, have been in talks to jointly pick up as much as $5 billion worth of Meta’s voting Class A shares.
Article Summary: N Nvidia to invest $3 billion into Meta's equity offering. The two tech giants will jointly develop Meta’s ‘Muse’ artificial intelligence (AI) assistant and refine the software running behind it. The investment forms part of an enormous capital drive by Meta, which raised the target for its latest equity offering to $97.5 billion.
